## Phase 155 / The `null` side of a protocol diagnostic had never run, and the pin that exercised it was itself the bug

- **Milestone / version:** test-only plus one `AGENTS.md` rule; no `src/` change, so nothing to release on its own. Branch `test/unknown-frame-normalization-v2` off `c995b40`; **PR #250**.
- **Status:** **open as PR #250 — CI running.** It supersedes #248, whose head is green (verify, browser, analyze, CodeQL) but predates the post reorder and this entry. #248 was rebased onto the merged `main`, and moving a rebased branch onto an open PR ref needs a force-push, which this repository does not do — so the change set moved to a new ref and #248 is closed with a pointer rather than rewritten.
- **The leg.** `handleMessage`'s `default:` arm does `this.lastUnknownMessageType = typeof unknown.type === 'string' ? unknown.type : null;`. The `null` side had never executed in any test, and `getUnknownMessageStats()` had **no reader at all** in `tests/` — so neither did the `unknownMessages` count that `getDiagnostics().protocol` publishes from it. The value is declared `string | null` and reaches consumers by name, which makes a forwarded number or a coerced `'[object Object]'` a consumer-visible contract break, not a cosmetic one.
- **The pin.** Four posts from a second channel joined *by name* (`${DEFAULT_STORAGE_PREFIX}:bus:${createOpaqueKey(clusterKey)}`), so the frames arrive through the same `createChannel` path a same-origin forger uses rather than by reaching into `handleMessage`. Each post is followed by a full `getUnknownMessageStats()` read, and the `onUnknownMessage` handler is asserted to have received all four raw frames in order — the counter is the only place the shape is judged, so an application collecting frames has to see what actually arrived.
- **The failure this PR shipped with, which is the more interesting half.** CI's `verify` died at `pnpm check`'s `tsc --noEmit` with two `TS2322`s: `postMessage({ type: 42 })` and `{ type: 'FUTURE_MESSAGE' }` are not assignable to `WorkerClusterMessage`, and **vitest never looks at types**, so the local `npx vitest run` that green-lit it could not have caught that. Fixed by widening once at the call site (`const postForged = (forged.postMessage as (message: unknown) => void).bind(forged)`) rather than per frame — `Object.create(null)` is `any`, so a per-frame cast would leave one of the four forged posts indistinguishable from a legal one. Now a rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Five mutants, and the order of the posts decides what they can report.** `String(unknown.type)` in place of the `typeof` guard does not merely report a wrong value for the prototype-less frame — it **throws** `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` out of `handleMessage`, through the fake channel, into the test's own stack. Measured first in a throwaway single-post probe (then deleted) because with the frames in their original order that mutant died one post earlier on the numeric value assertion, so the shipped test could not have surfaced the crash class at all. The prototype-less post therefore now leads. Kill map after the reorder, each at exactly one test: the leading post dies to a raw forward (`lastType: {}`), to the `String()` coercion (by the `TypeError`, at `cluster.ts:889`), to a `'non-string'` sentinel in place of `null`, and to dropping `unknownMessageCount += 1` (`count: +0`); the last post, the real string, is the only one that dies to `= null`. The `42` and bare-primitive posts have **no mutant of their own** — every variant that mishandles them mishandles a leading frame first — which the test comment says instead of implying four independent guards. Before the reorder the raw forward died at the `42` assertion, so the rotation moved a kill rather than adding one; what it added is the crash trace.
- **Coverage, re-derived rather than inherited:** `pnpm test:coverage` exits 0 at **99.02 / 96.98 / 99.27 / 99.69** on 910 tests, and `coverage/coverage-final.json` gives `cluster.ts` **20 zero branch slots of 399**. Both numbers confirm Phase 154's row (`96.93 → 96.98`, `21 → 20`), which had been written from the pre-reorder measurement.
- **One stale row corrected in the same commit:** Phase 154 cited #248's `verify` job as a fourth non-reproduction of the coordination sweep's unexplained red run. It was not one — that job failed on the two `TS2322`s above, so the sweep's capture count is three (#245, #246, #247).
- **Verification:** `pnpm check` 0 (typecheck, build, 910 tests, 5/5 perf gates) and `pnpm lint` 0, both re-run after the reorder; `pnpm test:coverage` 0 as above; `git diff --check` clean; five single-file mutation runs with `src/core/cluster.ts` restored by `git checkout --` after each. `verify:compat` / `verify:types` / `verify:pack` / `bench` / E2E are CI's on this PR's `verify` and `browser` jobs; nothing in `src/`, `dist/`, or the option surface moved here, so `verify:types`' baseline is definitionally unchanged.
- **Risk / rollback:** `git revert` of a test file plus two documentation rows; no behavior exists to roll back. The one residual risk is informational: the pin documents that a same-origin forger can push the diagnostic counter and the `lastType` field around, which is already the standing position on the unauthenticated cluster channel.
- **Next:** the ledger remainder as re-derived (`data-bus.ts` 12, `replay-manager.ts` 7, `replay-persistence.ts` 6, `cluster.ts`'s other 20, and the singletons in `websocket.ts` / `trace.ts` / `port-reaper.ts` / `centrifuge.ts` / `centrifuge-session.ts` / `validation.ts` / `version.ts`), then the idle-host `pnpm bench:browser` sample, now six releases stale.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 156 / Both halves of a partial option object, read one at a time

- **Milestone / version:** test-only; no `src/` change, so it rides the next patch rather than releasing on its own. Branch `test/persistence-retry-partial-defaults` off `fe360ca`; **PR #251**.
- **Status:** **open — CI running.**
- **The leg.** `assertPersistenceRetryOptions` validates `replay.persistenceRetry`'s two fields *only when present*, and `CrossTabDataBus` then supplies each default on its own (`maxAttempts ?? 1`, `backoffMs ?? 50`). The validator's "backoff omitted" fall-through had never completed: every partial object the suite builds (`{ maxAttempts: 0 }`, `{ maxAttempts: 1.5 }`, `{ backoffMs: -1 }`) throws at the field it names, so the leg that has to *accept* a partial policy was never reached. The coverage table read `validation.ts` at 100% lines with one zero branch arm (`[5, 0]`), and the 5 was every object that both supplied a backoff and survived the first check.
- **The trap in the aggregate number.** Both `??` sites look hot in coverage — 16804 left / 16768 right — and that is precisely what hides this: a bus with no `persistenceRetry` at all takes the right leg, and a bus with both fields takes the left, so "hot" says nothing about the one shape in between, where a config names *one* half. The defaults needed a test not because their counters were zero but because no counter distinguished "read the default" from "supplied the default's own value".
- **Two tests, one per default**, because each default is invisible to the other: `{ maxAttempts: 2 }` alone must wait the 50 ms backoff, and `{ backoffMs: 5 }` alone must not retry at all. The first is pinned by a **negative** assertion — exactly one `append` after a `setTimeout(0)`, then two after a longer wait — since a default that had collapsed to zero would already show the retry, and the file's existing zero-backoff cases prove both appends are visible by that point. The second needs no timing claim: the attempt ceiling is reached before the retry event is emitted.
- **Three mutants, disjoint kill sets, each at its own leg.** `?? 1` → `?? 2` dies at the second case alone (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`); `?? 50` → `?? 0` dies at the first case's named assertion; forcing the validator's guard true dies at the first case with `TypeError: replay.persistenceRetry.backoffMs must be a non-negative finite number.` at **1 failed / 911 passed**. That third one is the finding: an optional-field guard's failure mode is not a bad value slipping through, it is a **legal configuration being rejected**.
- **Two process catches worth keeping.** (1) `pnpm typecheck` failed the first draft with two `TS2345`s — collecting a `DataBusTraceEvent` union into an array of an *all-optional* shape trips TypeScript's weak-type rule (`Type 'DataBusLifecycleTraceEvent' has no properties in common`), and the file's existing recorder arrays already name a required `type: string` for exactly that reason. Vitest ran the file green. Same class as Phase 155's rule, arrived at from the other side, one release later. (2) The first mutation loop "killed" nothing because its `perl` patterns were regexes and the target text is full of regex syntax (`??`, `(`): three mutants were never created, and the empty `git diff` was the only thing that could have said so. Printing each mutant's diff before running it is now the first step, not a check afterwards.
- **Coverage, re-derived:** `pnpm test:coverage` exits 0; `validation.ts` is now **100 / 100 / 100 / 100** with its zero-arm count 1 → 0; `coverage/coverage-final.json` gives **59 zero branch slots of 1960** across `src/` (was 60 on `main`).
- **Deliberately *not* claimed as this PR's gain:** the aggregate branch percentage read **96.98** here and also read **96.98** on #250, because each PR lights one arm off the same `main`. This entry's first version inferred from that equality that "the pretty table cannot resolve a single arm", and that inference was **wrong** — see Phase 158, where the same arithmetic measured one arm at ~0.05 points and the table resolved it. What the aggregate genuinely cannot tell you is *which* arm moved, and that is the reason the per-slot count is cited here.
- **Verification:** `pnpm typecheck` 0 and `pnpm lint` 0 after the annotation fix; `pnpm test:coverage` 0 as above; three single-file mutation runs with `src/` restored by `git checkout --` after each; no `src/`, option, export or protocol change, so `verify:compat` / `verify:types` / `verify:pack` are untouched by construction. E2E is this PR's `browser` job.
- **Risk / rollback:** `git revert` of a test file and this entry; nothing executable moved.
- **Next:** the re-derived ledger is **58 zero arms** once #250 and this merge (`cluster.ts` 20, `data-bus.ts` 12, `replay-manager.ts` 7, `replay-persistence.ts` 6, `websocket.ts` 3, `trace.ts` 3, `port-reaper.ts` 3, `centrifuge.ts` 2, one each in `centrifuge-session.ts` and `version.ts`; `validation.ts` is closed). `version.ts`'s arm is already classified as statically dead in anything shipped, and `cluster.ts`'s remaining 20 are enumerated at their sites, so the next hunt is `data-bus.ts`'s 12 and `replay-manager.ts`'s 7. Then the idle-host `pnpm bench:browser` sample, now six releases stale.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 157 / The connect timer's staleness guard never runs, and the cancel it rests on was the unpinned half

- **Milestone / version:** one test plus a rewritten comment; no behavior change, so it rides the next patch. Branch `test/connect-timer-cancels-stale-attempt` off `7f052b1`; **PR #252**.
- **Status:** **merged — PR #252, `19ae34c`.** The gate counts below were measured on the pre-rebase tree (911 tests); the merged head ran 913 in that PR's `verify` job, which is the number the rebased tree should be judged against.
- **The leg.** `start()` arms a connect timer whose callback opens with `if (this.socket !== socket || this.handlers !== handlers || handshakeCompleted) return;`. Coverage gives zero hits for that early return's *consequent* — not one term, all three, in every run — and the site comment explained only `handshakeCompleted` ("cannot be reached today: `onopen` cancels this timer directly and again through `settleConnect()`"). The other two terms had no stated reason at all, which reads as "someone never wrote the test" rather than "no test can reach it".
- **The enumeration that closes it.** `this.socket` and `this.handlers` are reassigned in exactly two places, `start()` and `stop()`. Reaching either assignment inside `start()` requires the reuse guard at the top to fall through, i.e. `socketActive === false`, and every path that lowers `socketActive` has already cancelled the armed timer: `onclose` and `onerror` through `failConnect()`, `stop()` through `settleConnect()`, and this callback itself by nulling the handle as it fires. So no attempt can leave a timer armed behind it, and the guard has nothing to distinguish. That is why the arm is zero rather than thin.
- **The finding that made this worth opening.** The domination is a property of those cancels, not of the condition — and one of the cancels was unpinned. Deleting only `failConnect()`'s `clearConnectTimer()` left **the rest of the suite green** (910 tests at measurement). The consequence is not abstract: the dead attempt's own timeout then fires at `connectTimeoutMs` and reports a *second* failure — `onStatus('error')` plus an `onError('WebSocket did not open within Nms.')` — for a connection the application was already told had failed on the close. The new case pins exactly that pair, and dies at **1 of 911** on the mutant.
- **No coverage movement is claimed, deliberately.** `websocket.ts` still holds 3 zero branch arms of 123 after this change, and the aggregate is unchanged; the product here is a pin for a load-bearing cancel plus an unexplained zero arm converted into a stated invariant. Citing a coverage win would be false.
- **One numeric claim removed rather than refreshed.** The old comment asserted "deleting only that term leaves all 880 tests green". No current run has 880 tests, and the number carries no information a reader can act on, so the rewritten comment says "leaves the suite green" and this entry keeps the dated counts. Re-measured on this tree before deciding: the term-3-only mutant survives at the full suite, and the cancel-only mutant survives at 910 with this test absent.
- **Verification:** `pnpm check` 0 (typecheck, build, **911** tests, 5/5 perf gates), `pnpm lint` 0, `pnpm test:coverage` 0 at **99.02 / 96.98 / 99.27 / 99.69**, `git diff --check` clean, two mutation runs each with its one-line diff printed before the result was believed and `src/` restored by `git checkout --` after. No option, export or protocol change, so `verify:compat` / `verify:types` / `verify:pack` are untouched by construction; E2E is this PR's `browser` job.
- **Risk / rollback:** `git revert` of one test and one comment block. The test relies on fake timers and never advances the cluster clock, so it cannot leak a timer into another case; `vi.useRealTimers()` runs in the `finally`, matching the file's existing timer cases.
- **Next:** `data-bus.ts`'s 12 and `replay-manager.ts`'s 7 zero arms are the only sizeable un-enumerated groups left; `cluster.ts`'s remaining 20 carry site classifications, and `validation.ts` is closed. The `websocket.ts` singleton at `:121` (`this.connectPromise ?? undefined`) is now the most concrete open question in that file — it needs a live socket with a null gate, and whether any such state exists is an enumeration of `connectPromise`'s assignment sites, not a guess.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 158 / A TOKEN_REQUEST that names no channel, and the one fallback no frame ever reached

- **Milestone / version:** test-only, plus the correction below. Branch `test/channel-token-nameless-request-v2`; **PR #254**, which supersedes #253 for the reason Phase 155 records (#250 supersedes #248): the branch had to be rebased onto #252, and a rebased history cannot move onto an open PR ref without a force-push.
- **Status:** **open — CI running.**
- **The leg.** `resolveTokenRequest()` calls `provider.getChannelToken(channel ?? '')`, and the `''` fallback had **zero hits**: no frame the suite ever posted reached a `channelToken` request without a channel. That fallback is the only thing between a missing wire field and an application callback typed `(channel: string)`.
- **Why the nameless frame is a real shape, not a hypothesis.** `channel` is optional on the wire (`{ type: TOKEN_REQUEST; requestId; kind; channel?: string }` in `centrifuge-protocol.ts`), and the sender posts it with `...(channel === undefined ? {} : { channel })` — so a nameless request comes either from an older/foreign worker on the port or from **our own session**, because `getChannelToken: (channel: string) => this.requestToken('channelToken', lifecycle, channel)` trusts the argument the dependency hands it. The second route is why this is a receiver-trust question rather than a hardening exercise: the value crossing into application code is not produced by the code that validates it.
- **The pin.** `answers a channelToken request that names no channel with an empty one` emits the frame through the same `worker.emit()` path as the existing channel-token cases, asserts the provider was called with `''`, and asserts the posted `TOKEN_RESPONSE` carries the provider's own answer (`channel-token-`) — so the normalization is shown reaching the wire, not only the callback.
- **Mutation.** `channel ?? ''` → `channel as string`. Written in the form `tsc` accepts, because a bare `channel` would be a type error and a mutant that does not compile is not a caught mutant; the assertion is `provider.getChannelToken(channel: string)` and the field is `string | undefined`. The case fails on the call argument: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ '' ]`.
- **Correction to Phase 156, made by measuring rather than arguing.** That entry inferred from two sibling branches reading the same aggregate that "the pretty table cannot resolve a single arm". Re-measured on both sides of this change: `origin/main` reads **97.04** with **58** zero branch slots of 1960, this branch **97.09** with **57** — so one arm is ~0.05 points and the table resolves it. The equality it was reasoning from was equality of *deltas* (one arm off the same base, on both branches), which is arithmetic, not blindness. The real limitation stands as restated: the aggregate does not say *which* arm moved.
- **One derived number admitted.** This PR's commit message cited `97.04` for `main` before `main` had been measured, deriving it from the per-arm step. The derivation happened to be right, and the table above is the measurement that makes the claim good; the lesson is the one already on the record — a number that came out of arithmetic has to be labelled as such or measured.
- **Verification:** `pnpm check` 0 (typecheck, build, **914** tests, 5/5 perf gates) and `pnpm test:coverage` 0 on this branch; `pnpm test:coverage` 0 at **97.04** on `origin/main` for the comparison above; one mutation run, its one-line diff printed before the result was believed, `src/` restored by `git checkout --` afterwards. No `src/`, option, export or protocol change, so `verify:compat` / `verify:types` / `verify:pack` are untouched by construction. The count read **913** before this branch was rebased onto #252 and **914** after — the same trap Phase 157 records for its own row, arriving twice in one session because a rebase silently changes the denominator of every measurement written before it.
- **A worktree detour worth recording:** the first attempt to measure `main` used `git worktree add` + a symlinked `node_modules`, and 11 tests failed there — all of them `dual-format` / `verify-packed-consumer`, which read `dist/` and have no artifact in a fresh worktree. That is a harness gap, not a red `main`, and reading it as the latter would have invented a regression. Measured in the real tree instead, where `dist/` matches the branch's `src/`.
- **Risk / rollback:** `git revert` of one test and these rows. The residual question this entry does *not* close: with `centrifuge@5.7.4` installed, the client-level hook the library documents is `getToken`, and a prior probe found no `getChannelToken` in that build's client config — so how often the `channelToken` kind is produced by the dependency at all is an open question about the dependency, not about this repository. The `TOKEN_REQUEST` bridge is ours and stays pinned either way.
- **Next:** `centrifuge.ts` is down to its already-classified `startHeartbeat()` guard. `websocket.ts` keeps three zero arms: the early return #252 classifies, the reuse path's `this.connectPromise ?? undefined` (which needs an enumeration of `connectPromise`'s three assignment sites, not a test), and one `if` whose branch region carries no location. Then the larger groups: `data-bus.ts` 12, `replay-manager.ts` 7, `replay-persistence.ts` 6 (four of them the `settled` latches, recorded as dominated-in-effect), `cluster.ts` 20 (site-classified), `trace.ts` 3, `port-reaper.ts` 3.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 159 / Three of four legs of a Blob conversion, and the one that kept a dead socket from speaking

- **Milestone / version:** test-only; no behavior change, so it rides the patch this batch closes. Branch `test/blob-conversion-failure-after-replacement` off `adefda4`; **PR pending from that branch**.
- **Status:** **open — first push, so no superseded ref this time** (see the workflow row).
- **The leg.** `handleMessage`'s Blob branch awaits `raw.arrayBuffer()` and reports a failure only through `if (this.socket === socket && this.handlers === handlers && this.socketActive)`. Three of its four legs had tests: a Blob that resolves on the live connection, a Blob that *resolves* after the connection was replaced, and a conversion that fails on the live connection. The fourth — a conversion that fails after the connection was replaced — had never executed, so the **swallow** was unasserted.
- **Why the swallow is the interesting one.** The report on the next line goes to `this.handlers`, i.e. whoever holds the connection *at that moment*, not the one whose frame failed. Delete the guard and a dead socket's conversion error is delivered to the replacement connection's `onError` — which a user reads as "the new connection is broken", on a connection that is fine.
- **The pin.** `does not report a Blob conversion failure that belongs to a replaced connection`: open a socket, deliver a Blob whose `arrayBuffer` is a deferred rejection, `stop()` + `start()` with fresh handlers, *then* reject. Asserts the new connection's `onError` and `onMessage` both stay silent.
- **Mutation.** Forcing the guard to `if (true)` — a form `tsc` accepts, which is the requirement (the mutant must compile or it is not a caught mutant) — fails exactly one test of **914**, this one, with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments… but actually been called 1 times`. `src/websocket.ts` restored by `git checkout --` afterwards.
- **Coverage:** `websocket.ts` 3 → 2 zero branch slots of 123; across `src/` **56 of 1960** (was 57 on `19ae34c`). Aggregate **99.02 / 97.14 / 99.27 / 99.69** on **915** tests. This is also the first entry where Phase 158's corrected reading was applied rather than re-derived wrong: the number was measured again *after* the rebase, because the rebase moved the base by a test and an arm and every figure written before it belonged to the older tree.
- **Workflow, the rule from #254 used on purpose:** this commit was made locally, held while #254's CI ran, and rebased onto `adefda4` **before its first push**. Rebasing an already-pushed branch is what forced the superseding refs for #250 and #254, so the order is now: commit → wait for the anchor-touching PR to merge → rebase → push once. No PR was burned.
- **Verification:** `pnpm test:coverage` 0 (915 tests) on the rebased tree, `pnpm check` 0 on the pre-rebase tree (914) and re-run after — see the row above — one mutation run with its one-line diff printed first, `git diff --check` clean. No `src/`, option, export or protocol change, so `verify:compat` / `verify:types` / `verify:pack` are untouched by construction; E2E is this PR's `browser` job.
- **Risk / rollback:** `git revert` of one test. The test controls the rejection itself and never leaves a promise unhandled, so it cannot produce the "all green, coverage run exits 1 on an unhandled rejection" failure mode recorded for the persistence tests.
- **Next:** `websocket.ts` is down to two arms, both written up: `:178` (the connect-timer staleness guard, classified in Phase 157) and `:121` (`this.connectPromise ?? undefined`, whose question is whether anything can re-enter `start()` between storing the socket and storing the gate — an enumeration, not a test). Then `data-bus.ts` 12, `replay-manager.ts` 7, `replay-persistence.ts` 6, `cluster.ts` 20, `trace.ts` 3, `port-reaper.ts` 3. This batch (#250, #251, #252, #254, and this) is test-only plus one rewritten `src/` comment, which ships through the bundles, so it closes as a patch release once it merges.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 162 / The two capability checks that a partial adapter was never asked to make

- **Milestone / version:** test-only, first work after `0.21.18`. Branch `test/replay-capability-absent-adapters` off `29b6715`.
- **Status:** **open — first push.**
- **The legs.** `clearAll()` and `clearBefore()` both put their durable operation behind an optional-method check — `this.persistence?.clear ? withPersistenceRetry(…) : null`, and the same for `clearBefore`. `DataBusReplayPersistence` makes both methods optional, so an adapter that implements only `load`/`append` is legal, and **neither `: null` leg had ever executed**: every case in `tests/replay-manager.test.ts` either injected a full adapter or issued one `clearBefore` per lifecycle.
- **Why the `Math.max` leg is the one with teeth.** `hydrationClearBefore` filters **what `load()` returns**, not what the store holds. With an adapter that has no `clearBefore`, nothing is pruned durably, so the filter is the only enforcement of a cutoff the caller already asked for — and two cutoffs in one lifecycle is exactly where last-write-wins differs from newest-wins. Replacing the max with `timestamp` re-hydrates a message the application had cleared: `expected [ 2, 3 ] to deeply equal [ 3 ]`, one test failing out of 65.
- **Why the `clear` leg fails in the other direction.** Degrading `this.persistence?.clear` to `this.persistence` keeps the code compiling (`clear!()` already asserts) and makes an operation that had *nothing durable to do* reject with `TypeError: this.persistence.clear is not a function` after the retry budget — a caller-visible failure of a successful local clear. Both mutants were run against the whole file, each dying at exactly one test, each with its diff printed first.
- **The regex trap, caught the second time in one session.** The `clear` mutant was first applied with a multi-line `perl -0pi -e 's/\Q…\E/…/'` that matched nothing; the run then reported "65 passed" and read as a surviving mutant. The tell is the printed diff being **empty**, and it is now the first thing checked before a mutant result is believed — the same failure Phase 156 recorded for a single-line pattern. The applied edit was then made through an editor call, not a regex.
- **Coverage:** `replay-manager.ts` 7 → **5** zero branch slots; the two that closed are `:214` (`clearAll`'s `: null`) and `:254` (`clearBefore`'s `: null`). Across `src/` **54 of 1960** (was 56 at `0.21.18`). All five survivors already carry a site comment, and they are three different kinds: `:418` (`hydrate`'s `!this.buffers || !this.persistence`) and `:525` (`scheduleRetentionCleanup`'s `!this.persistence?.clearBefore`) are dominated-by-caller capability checks — note they are *not* the two legs this unit closed, which is easy to conflate since all four read as "optional persistence method"; `:433` and `:573` are the generation re-checks; `:486` is the `PersistenceRetryCancelledError` wrap enumerated on 2026-09-23.
- **Verification:** `pnpm check` 0 (typecheck, build, **917** tests, 5/5 perf gates) and `pnpm test:coverage` 0 on the **rebased** tree — the rule from Phase 158 applied deliberately rather than learned again; `pnpm lint` 0; `git diff --check` clean; no `src/` change survives the branch (the two mutant runs both ended in `git checkout -- src/core/replay-manager.ts`).
- **Risk / rollback:** `git revert` of one test file. Neither test advances a timer or touches a clock, so no scheduler coupling is introduced.
- **Next:** `replay-persistence.ts`'s 6 (four are the `settled` latches recorded as dominated-in-effect, leaving `:233` and one location-less `if`), `data-bus.ts`'s 12, and the singletons in `trace.ts` / `port-reaper.ts` / `centrifuge-session.ts` / `version.ts`. `cluster.ts`'s 20 all carry site text, so the next hunt should start where a site comment is *absent*, not where a counter is zero.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 163 / The clamp that clamps nothing: one bad clock reading blanked a whole metrics window

- **Milestone / version:** first `src/` behavior change since `0.21.18`, and patch material. Branch `fix/trace-latency-sample-integrity` off `30b2f7e`.
- **The leg.** `recordDispatched()` counted every dispatch with a matching receive as a latency sample. `trace.now` is a public, documented option, so the clock is consumer code, and `Math.max(0, this.now() - receivedTimestamp)` — the clamp added for a *backwards* clock — passes `NaN` straight through, because `Math.max` returns `NaN` if any argument is `NaN`. The sample count still rose while the bucket write landed on the non-index property `"NaN"`, which no percentile walk can reach: it iterates `0 … buckets.length - 1`.
- **Measured on the unmodified reporter** (throwaway probe file, one 50 ms sample plus one NaN-delay sample, deleted once the numbers were in hand): `dispatchSamples: 2`, `dispatchAvgMs: NaN` — which `JSON.stringify` renders as `null`, so the field disappears rather than reading wrong — and `dispatchP95Ms`/`dispatchMaxMs` both pinned at the histogram ceiling because the rank exceeds the sum of every reachable bucket, while `dispatchP50Ms: 75` still printed a plausible number. Control run with the second reading at `-150 ms` instead: avg 25, p50 25, p95 75, max 75, everything coherent. **That asymmetry is the fix's shape** — an out-of-order pair is a real measurement that clamps to 0, an unmeasurable one is not a sample at all, which is already what the "no matching receive" path above it means.
- **The change.** `if (!Number.isFinite(delayMs)) return;` before anything is recorded, clamp moved after it. Both non-finite kinds (`NaN`, `±Infinity`) drop the sample; `received`, `dispatched` and `topics` still count the dispatch, and the JSDoc now says a dispatch whose delay cannot be computed produces no sample.
- **Two tests, disjoint kill sets.** `records no latency sample when the injected clock answers a dispatch read with a non-finite value` loops `NaN`/`+Infinity`/`-Infinity` with a `clock reading …` message on every assertion so a loop failure names its case, and `keeps counting a measurable dispatch whose clock ran backwards` is the control. Three mutants, three distinct results: deleting the guard dies only in the first test; replacing `isFinite` with `isNaN` dies at `clock reading Infinity: expected 2 to be 1`; replacing `Math.max(0, delayMs)` with `delayMs` dies only in the second, at `expected -50 to be 25`. Each mutant's diff was printed before its result was read, and each run ended in `git checkout -- src/core/trace.ts`.
- **The sweep that came with it.** Six arms outside `cluster.ts`/`data-bus.ts` had read 0 with nothing at the site explaining why, so every coverage pass re-hunted them. Now recorded: `websocket.ts`'s `connectPromise ?? undefined` (excluded by the field's whole write set, and needed for the type anyway), `replay-persistence.ts`'s `dbPromise === pending` fall-through (no writer fits between a rejection and the first reaction on that promise), `port-reaper.ts`'s null-handle arm (unreachable, not merely unreached, because `dispose()` clears the maps every caller is gated on and has no Worker-side caller), and three `invalidate`+`reject` latches in `clear`/`clearTopic`/`clearBefore` that now point at the enumeration which already covered all four of them but sat only in `load()`.
- **A new tier, and why three of those arms are uncloseable.** `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on, so an index read is `T | undefined` whether or not a hole is reachable, and the fallback that satisfies the assignment can neither run nor be deleted. Measured rather than argued: `this.latencyBuckets[bucketIndex] += 1` is `TS2532`, `return this.connectPromise` is `TS2322`, `export const SDK_VERSION: string = __SDK_VERSION__` is `TS2322`. Written up as an AGENTS.md rule next to the two tiers it already names, because "hunt where a counter is zero" sends a reader to these legs forever.
- **Coverage:** `src/` **54 of 1962** zero branch slots, against 54 of 1960 at `0.21.18` — the new `if` contributes two slots and both are covered, so **no arm closed and none opened**; the denominator moved and the numerator did not. `trace.ts` keeps its three, each now labelled with which kind it is. Aggregate `99.02 / 97.24 / 99.27 / 99.69`.
- **Verification:** `pnpm check` 0 (typecheck, build, **919** tests, 5/5 perf gates), `pnpm test:coverage` 0 and `verify:compat` / `verify:types` / `verify:pack` 0, all on the **rebased** tree; `pnpm lint` 0.
- **Host note:** `pnpm bench:browser` deferred for a ninth consecutive release — sampled load `90.51 / 86.49 / 68.05` with `WindowServer` at 85.8% and a headless Chrome at 59.5%, i.e. the archive would gain a loaded sample that the gate's own ceiling then has to tolerate.
- **Risk / rollback:** one early `return` in a diagnostics path; reverting the `fix(trace): drop an unmeasurable latency sample instead of recording it` commit restores the old window. No frame, default, storage key or export moved, so the three public-surface gates see nothing. The consumer-visible difference is that a metrics window whose clock misbehaves now reports finite numbers instead of a missing average.
- **Next:** the same tier question applied to `cluster.ts`'s 20 and `data-bus.ts`'s 12 — both already carry site text, so the value there is a per-arm re-read asking *which* of the four verdicts each is (type artifact / dominated / only handler / reached-but-redundant), not another hunt.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 164 / The two publish shapes no test had ever sent

- **Milestone / version:** test-only plus one repository rule, first work after `0.21.19`. Branch `test/publish-shapes-never-sent` off `f41fb34`.
- **The legs.** `WorkerClusterRuntime.publish` declares two overloads — `(topic, data, messageId: string)` and `(topic, data, metadata)` — and the string form's normalization (`typeof metadataOrMessageId === 'string' ? { messageId: metadataOrMessageId } : metadataOrMessageId`) had never executed. `CrossTabDataBus.publish` always hands over an object, so nothing reachable *through the bus* can take that arm, and no test called the runtime directly with a string — even though `docs/api.md` tells callers that coordinate directly to use this class. The same one-sided reading sat in `publishBatch()`'s single-item delegation: every case in the suite supplied **both** `messageId` and `timestamp`, so the `… || …` test, its `: undefined` fallback, and both `!== undefined ? { x } : {}` spreads had each only ever been evaluated one way.
- **Five branch slots closed.** `cluster.ts` 20 → **15** zero arms; across `src/` **54 → 49 of 1962**; aggregate branches **97.24 → 97.50**. That is the largest single-pass movement in this ledger series, and it came from two calls no test had ever made rather than from a harder-to-reach guard.
- **Which leg has teeth, and which only has coverage.** The absent-metadata case is the only one of the five with a distinct consequence: `sendControl` calls the handler with **three** arguments when `metadata` is falsy and five otherwise, so the arity is what separates "this publication arrived without an id" from "it arrived with an id of `undefined`". Mutants, each diff printed first: drop the string normalization (`? {…}` → `? undefined`) → dies at the new overload test, 1 failing of 96; replace the `: undefined` fallback with `: {}` → dies at `expected last "vi.fn()" call to have been called with [ 'PUBLISH', 'feed.partial', 1 ]`, 1 failing of 96; replace the two conditional spreads with always-present keys → **96/96 green**, because the receiving side re-normalizes with `metadata?.x === undefined ? {} : …`, so an omitted key and an `undefined` value produce the same wire frame.
- **…and why those two partial legs still cannot be simplified away.** The always-keys mutant fails `pnpm check` with `TS2769`: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on, so `{ messageId: string | undefined }` is not assignable to `{ messageId?: string }`. That makes them the same tier as the `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` legs found in Phase 163 — uncloseable from both ends, unreachable by any assertion at this seam and undeletable by the compiler — which is now written into `AGENTS.md` next to that rule rather than left as a second discovery for the next reader.

## Phase 166 / A namespace alias the isolation sentence did not name, and the first cluster arm whose fallback the compiler does not need

- **Milestone / version:** test + shipped-prose correction, first work after the `0.21.19` record. Branch `test/cluster-arm-tiers` off `3f71715`.
- **The leg.** The cluster namespace is `createOpaqueKey(options.clusterKey || '__default__')`, so an **empty** `clusterKey` is not its own cluster — it hashes the literal string and shares storage keys and the BroadcastChannel with `'__default__'`. `clusterKey` is a required, unvalidated `string`, so `''` is the only way to reach that arm, and nothing in the suite had taken it. Meanwhile both the option's own JSDoc and `AGENTS.md` said different cluster keys "operate in isolation" with no exception named — an absolute about behavior, which is the shape that has produced shipped-doc defects before.
- **The pin.** Two runtimes on one storage + hub, one keyed `''` and one keyed `'__default__'`, subscribe the same topic: exactly one of them owns it (asserted as `['empty-key']`, so the assertion names *which* and also holds stickiness). The control half is a third runtime on `'another-namespace'`, which owns its own copy of the same topic name. That second half is what makes the test fail if the fallback ever widens beyond the empty string.
- **Mutation.** `||` → `??` (which keeps `''` as its own namespace) reddens exactly the new case: `expected [ 'empty-key', 'default-name' ] to deeply equal [ 'empty-key' ]`, 1 failing of 97, diff printed before the result was read, restored with `git checkout -- src/core/cluster.ts`.
- **The tier question, answered per arm instead of by counter.** Every remaining falsifiable arm in the route-write block was probed by deleting its fallback and running `tsc`: `?? worker.load` (two sites), `(projectedLoads.get(…) ?? owner.load) + 1`, `?? this.currentRecord` (two sites) and `route?.workerId ?? this.workerId` all **fail to compile** without the fallback (`TS2345`/`TS2532`/`TS18048` at the consumer), so they are the uncloseable tier `AGENTS.md` now describes. `(previous?.generation ?? 0)` is the one that **compiles bare** — `WorkerRoute.generation` is a required `number` — so its zero count is owned by a different line: the `previous?.workerId !== this.workerId` filter three lines above takes every null `previous` out of the loop, because `undefined` never equals a worker id. Written at the site, because in a coverage report the two look identical and are not.
- **Coverage:** `cluster.ts` 15 → **14** zero arms, across `src/` **49 → 48 of 1962**, aggregate branches **97.50 → 97.55**; 922 tests.
- **Verification:** `pnpm check` 0 and `pnpm test:coverage` 0 measured on the tree before the rebase (which brought in only the `0.21.19` progress record) and re-run after it; `pnpm lint` 0; `git diff --check` clean.
- **Risk / rollback:** one test, two source comments, one `AGENTS.md` clause; `git revert` of the single commit removes all of it. No behavior changed — the alias is documented as it is, not fixed, because moving `''` to its own namespace would silently relocate storage for anyone already passing an empty key.
- **Next:** `data-bus.ts`'s 12 arms get the same delete-and-compile treatment, which is the only way left to find out how many of them are the uncloseable tier rather than unasserted behavior.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 168 / A wait whose deletion is invisible to every ordering test, and loud everywhere else

- **Milestone / version:** test + shipped-comment work after `0.21.20`. Branch `test/queued-start-no-stop-gate` off `d62eacb`.
- **The leg.** `queueStartAfterStop()`'s `this.stopPromise ?? Promise.resolve()` had never taken its fallback operand. That operand is the state *a failed initial open* lives in: its teardown is owned by `pendingStop`, so no `stopPromise` exists, and nothing reachable through a browser re-enters `start()` inside that `stopping` window — the only synchronous application-code seam there is the caller's own `ClusterEnvironment` port (a `localStorage.removeItem` never calls back). So the pin wraps the port: a storage write that re-enters `bus.start({})` during the cleanup, which is the port's contract rather than a browser page.
- **What the ordering assertion turned out NOT to pin, measured.** The test asserts the transport call order `start` (fails) → `stop` → `start` (succeeds). Replacing the whole read with `const stop = Promise.resolve()` leaves all 194 tests in the file green, and so does moving the `pendingStop` installation below the `cluster.stop()` window: `start()` chains the reopen behind `this.pendingStop` independently, so the order survives both. The first version of this branch's comment claimed the second mutation was what the test exists to fail. It is not, and the claim was replaced with the measurement.
- **Where that mutation actually lands: a worker OOM with zero failed tests.** With the read deleted, a restart that wakes early calls `start()`, which re-queues because `stopping` is still true — one microtask per turn, forever, starving the macrotask the transport's async stop needs. `pnpm test` goes red with `Tests 922 passed (923)` and `Errors 1 error`: `tests/lifecycle-invariants.test.ts` aborts its fork ~40 s in with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit` and a native stack inside `Builtins_RunMicrotasks`. So the guard is load-bearing and its witness is the fuzz, not any assertion — and the reason no assertion can replace it is the reason the candidate below had to go.
- **A candidate test deleted on its own measurement.** A second case was written and committed: queue a restart behind a `FakeTransport.stopGate`, assert no reopen while the gate is held, release, assert exactly one. It passes with the read deleted (and with `start()`'s `pendingStop` gate deleted, and with both) because a bounded number of `await Promise.resolve()` turns cannot observe a livelock that only ends when the *timer* queue gets a turn. Four single-leg mutations tried, zero killed → characterization, so it was removed from the branch (the commit was dropped before anything was pushed) and its zero kill rate written into the site comment instead.
- **What the shipped test does have teeth on.** Routing `start()` on the gate instead of the flag (`if (this.stopping)` → `if (this.stopPromise)`) reddens it, as an escaped `Transport failed during startup.` from the fresh-open path it would then take. Measured against that one mutation: exactly this case plus the pre-existing "performs a fresh stop when the previous stop gate is settled but not yet cleared" fail, 192 pass.
- **Ledger.** `data-bus.ts` 12 → **11** zero arms, `src/` **48 → 47 of 1962**, aggregate branches **97.55 → 97.60**, 923 tests. The closed arm now reads `[87, 1]`: 87 of the 88 calls to that method took the gate operand, one took the fallback. `:586`'s dedupe consequent is still `[0, 87]`, which is the measurement that keeps the "unreachable from the only caller" sentence above it honest.
- **Two repository rules from it, in `AGENTS.md`.** (1) Before writing a guard off as unpinnable, ask whether deleting it changes *when* work happens rather than *what* it produces; for the former, name the fuzz as the witness at the site instead of adding a test that looks like coverage. (2) A candidate test that survives every single-leg mutation around it is characterization, not a pin — delete it and record the measurement.
- **Verification:** `pnpm test:coverage` 0 on the committed tree; each mutation restored with `git checkout -- src/core/data-bus.ts` after its run, with the diff printed before the result was read; the compiler leg re-measured (`TS18047` on the bare field). `pnpm check` / `pnpm lint` results are recorded in the PR.
- **Risk / rollback:** one test, three comment blocks in `src/core/data-bus.ts`, one `AGENTS.md` bullet; no behavior change, so mixed-version peers and the three public-surface gates see nothing.
- **Next:** `cluster.ts`'s 14 remaining arms are all site-commented, so the productive question there is no longer "which tier" but "which site comment is stale" — a re-read of each comment's enumeration against the current code. `replay-persistence.ts`'s 6 are next in size order.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.

## Phase 169 / Three kinds of stale comment: a count that read as a description, a measurement that no longer reproduces, and line numbers nobody can see rot

- **Milestone / version:** shipped-prose correction, no behavior change. Branch `docs/cluster-arm-claims` off `edf5aa9`.
- **The claim.** `subscribe()`'s note said "`reconcileSubscriptions()` holds **the identical pair** for the same reason. Deleting **both** fallbacks leaves the suite green…", and the handoff-block note referred to "the **two** `?? this.currentRecord` **pairs**". `grep -c "?? this.currentRecord" src/core/cluster.ts` answers three: one in `subscribe()`, and **two** inside `reconcileSubscriptions()` — its invalidated-route leg and its stale-handoff re-election. So the sentence was not merely imprecise, it was a count that no longer matched the file, and the consequence was worse than the wording: the stale-handoff fallback carried **no site text**, which also retires Phase 162's "every remaining `cluster.ts` arm has a note at its site".
- **Re-measured per site, one deletion at a time, with `tsc --noEmit`.** `subscribe()`'s → 3 rejections (`writeRoute(…, owner, …)` as `WorkerRecord | undefined`, then `owner.workerId` twice); the route leg → 2 (same pair of shapes); the stale-handoff leg → **7** (its projected-load `set` at three positions, three further `owner.workerId` reads, its own `writeRoute`). Those counts are now at the three sites, and the phrase "identical pair" is gone, because a count is checkable in a way a description is not.
- **What came out of the same sweep as correct, recorded so nobody re-hunts it.** `assignedTopics` is "grown by exactly three writers" — three `.set` call sites, no more. The `if (!owner) continue;` note's "fails `tsc --noEmit` five times: three on `projectedLoads.set(...)`, one on `writeRoute`, one on `sendRouteReleased`" reproduces exactly (line 535 three positions, 545 `TS2345`, 553). "`publishBatch()` is the only sender of `items`" holds in the frame sense: it is the only site that puts `items` into a `sendControl` call, and the sibling mention is the receiver's shape guard. And the `?? 0` generation note is right that it is the odd one out — it is the only one of the block's three fallbacks that compiles bare.
- **The second find: a measurement quoted in prose that no longer reproduces.** `reopenTransport()`'s absorb note said "forcing `pending` to reject fails exactly one test … whether this line is present or deleted". Re-measured four ways on this tree, against the 194-test file: delete the absorb alone → 194/194 green; force `pending` to reject at that seam with the absorb intact → 194/194; the same forcing with the absorb deleted → **51 failed**; keep the absorb and add only the forcing's extra `.then` link → 194/194. So the sentence was wrong in both halves, and the replacement argues the same conclusion harder: nothing in an ordinary run notices that guard, and its deletion under a violated premise is not one diagnosable failure but a third of the file going down with it. The phase entry that first recorded the number is left standing as history and retracted here rather than rewritten — the comment in `src/core/data-bus.ts` is now the authority.
- **The third find is a class, not a sentence: line-number citations inside comments rot where nothing can see them.** Dumping every `:NNN` reference in `src/` beside the line it points at (`cites :N -> <line N>`, ten lines of script) found **six of the eleven** own-file citations wrong and one imprecise: `centrifuge-session.ts`'s `assertPublicTopic` trio (`data-bus.ts:929`, `:1009`, `:1033`) had drifted ~27 lines onto a blank line and a docstring opener; `replay-manager.ts`'s two references into `withPersistenceRetry` (`:565-567`, `:568`) landed *inside another comment*, because the two generation checks moved to `:572`/`:577` and the raw rethrow to `:583` after a block was inserted above the function; and `resetBuffers()`'s epoch bump was cited at its own docstring three lines early. All seven now name the symbol or the condition instead. Of the four that were correct, two were converted anyway and two left numbered; the four that must stay numbered are the dependency's (`types.d.ts:126`, `build/index.js:762` and `:162`, `BaseSubscription` at `:667-2674`) — re-verified against the installed `centrifuge@5.7.4`, including that the class really does hold exactly twelve `emit('error')` sites — because those name a pinned version rather than our moving file. `AGENTS.md` carries the rule and the audit's shape.
- **Proof that a prose sweep touched no code, and it is cheap.** Run `npx esbuild --loader=ts` over each changed file at HEAD and at `origin/main` and `cmp` the output: identical emitted JS for all five files. That is a stronger statement than counting `//` prefixes, which is what the diff review had been going on, and it costs one loop.
- **Method.** For a count inside a comment, grep the **symbol** the count is about, not the sentence — `?? this.currentRecord` finds all three copies, while "identical pair" finds only the one paragraph that says it. That is the existing paraphrase rule applied to numbers rather than prose, and it is what surfaced the undocumented site.
- **Verification:** `pnpm typecheck` 0, `pnpm lint` 0, `pnpm check` 0 (build, **923** tests, 5/5 perf gates) and `git diff --check` clean, all on the final tree; the phase spans five source files plus `AGENTS.md` and this log, and the esbuild comparison above is what establishes that none of it moved code. Each probe restored its file byte-identically in the script's own `finally`, whose last printed line is that assertion, so a partial restore invalidates the report rather than poisoning it.
- **Risk / rollback:** comments and one repository rule; `git revert` removes the phase. Comment text ships (declarations *and* bundles), so the consumer-visible difference is prose only — no frame, default, storage key, export or behavior moved, which is why the three public-surface gates have nothing to report.
- **Next:** the citation and count sweep still owes a pass over `trace.ts`, `port-reaper.ts`, `version.ts`, `worker-mode.ts` and the two adapter entries (`hooks.ts`, `vue.ts`) — the grep for numeric / `only` / `exactly` phrasing found no checkable claim in any of those — while the same grep's hits in `websocket.ts` ("assigned in exactly two statements"), `centrifuge.ts` and `storage-batch.ts` (the only-caller and the retry-cancel pair) all verified correct, all verified correct, as did the two references to our own files deliberately left numbered (`storage-batch.ts`'s flush-gate `:99`, and `routing.ts:64-70` from `validation.ts`). So the remaining question there is absolutes rather than counts. Then the ledger's next real target is `replay-persistence.ts`'s six, four of which are the `settled` latches already classified.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-24.
