## Phase 190 / 0.21.28 prepared: four comment sites, and the measurements behind them taken again rather than carried forward

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.28` prepared, not yet tagged. Branch `docs/reopen-handler-enumeration`, cut from main at `37c6b02` (the `0.21.27` record), rebased onto it after `#289` merged. Six commits: `ba7b678` (`data-bus`: reopen absorb → caller list), `cc80498` (`environment`: monotonic-clock retraction), `fac5ced` (`workers`: `ReapTarget` ordering), `8ee3f11` (`data-bus`: census row encoding + re-derivation), `2ea8dc2` (`data-bus`: operand kill counts re-run), `d622f43` (release prep: version, CHANGELOG, roadmap en/zh, `AGENTS.md`). Aggregate over `git diff --numstat origin/main..HEAD -- src/`: 3 files, +58/−21, and the comment-filtered diff of that range returns nothing.
- **What the release carries.** No code. Two of the four sentences were false, one was true but undecodable, one was true and ungrammatical:
  1. `reopenTransport()`'s early-return `.catch` justified itself as "the only handler this opening ever gets … not dominated by anything: it is the handler". Five sites call the method; three (`startDemandRecovery()`, `updateStatus()`'s recovery-timer arm, `runTransport()`) chain their own `opening.then(f, g)` onto the same object, so `g` is already a handler of `opening` and this line decides nothing there; `start()` returns it to its caller. Only `resumeTransport()`'s `void` call needs it. The note now says that, and records the symmetric mutation (deleting **this** line, or the `.catch` at the top of the method, each leaves 37 files green with zero unhandled-rejection reports) so the distinction reads as an enumeration rather than a pin.
  2. `ClusterEnvironment.now` said "the injected clock is the only monotonic one in the picture". False twice: `createBrowserEnvironment` binds the field to `Date.now` and no monotonic source (`performance.now()`, `hrtime`) is read anywhere in `src/`; and the injected clocks are not monotonic by contract either. Rewritten as the consumer property that is actually load-bearing — `cluster.ts` is the field's only reader in `src/`, ten reads, seven of which only stamp a record (`heartbeatAt`/`registeredAt`/route `updatedAt`/`confirmedAt`/subscriber `updatedAt`), while the three that subtract (`isStaleHandoff`, `readWorkers`, `cleanupOrphanedRoutes`) each fail their comparison on a backwards jump, so a pre-jump stamp survives until the clock climbs back past it; `sampleThroughput`, given the same reading as `heartbeatAt`, returns no sample instead of a negative window.
  3. `runTransport()`'s guard note quoted census rows `1000`/`0000`/`0100`/`1001`/`1010` and never said the bits are its four premises in source order — so no reader could check any of them. Encoding stated, instrument named, row set re-derived.
  4. `ReapTarget`'s "a port that is about to be closed is the only chance its owner gets to learn why" — a port is not a chance. Now names the three steps, the order, why `notify` precedes `close`, and what the shared `try`/`catch` costs a target that throws in `notify`.
- **Measurements taken for this entry, not inherited.** (a) The census re-run (first-sight `console.log` per distinct row, one whole-suite run): **same five rows**, and the `1001` origin is now the stack itself — `handoffAssignedTopics()` → `onControl` → `unsubscribeTransport()` — which is what the sentence previously paraphrased. (b) The two operand mutants re-run against the full suite: `droppedAfterConnect` still dies to **exactly its two named tests** (`parks every operation behind a demanded reopen…`, `reopens a cleanly disconnected transport…`); `transportReady` dies to **nine** (6 `data-bus.test.ts`, 3 `centrifuge.test.ts`) where the note said eight — and the eight were never named, so the newcomer is unidentifiable. Both numbers are now written as "run the mutant". (c) A clock census over every `now:` arrow body in `tests/` and `e2e/` (the sources in use are `now`, `clock`, `clock.now`, `Date.now()` and literals): exactly one test steps its clock backwards, deliberately — `tests/trace.test.ts`'s "keeps counting a measurable dispatch whose clock ran backwards". (d) The ledger re-derived from fresh `coverage/coverage-final.json`: **46 zero-count arms of 1963**, with the per-file distribution unchanged from `0.21.27` (`cluster` 13, `data-bus` 11, `replay-persistence` 6, `replay-manager` 5, `trace` 3, `port-reaper` 3, `websocket` 2, `centrifuge-session` 1, `centrifuge` 1, `version` 1) — that identity is the control that makes "comment-only" a measurement.
- **`AGENTS.md`** gained the two general rules next to the existing decay bullet: a flag vector must state its encoding and its re-derivation instrument, and a kill count carries its list or carries the instruction to re-run the mutant ("at least N" does not save it, because a reader cannot tell a grew-from list from a complete one).
- **Verification (pre-tag, this tree):** `pnpm check` 0 — typecheck, build, **936** tests / 37 files, 5/5 perf gates. `pnpm lint` 0. `pnpm test:coverage` 0, aggregate 99.02 / 97.65 / 99.27 / 99.69, floors met. `npx vitest run tests/documentation.test.ts` 18/18 (phase-number uniqueness, en/zh parity, single `## Next candidates` anchor). `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.28 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` 0. `pnpm build` 0, then `verify:compat` ("0.21.28 preserves public exports and type metadata from `v0.21.27`"), `verify:types` ("6 entries, 90 importable names, surface closed, nothing dropped since `v0.21.27`") and `verify:pack` all 0 — these three run at the bumped version, so the comparison is genuinely cross-version. `pnpm bench` 0 (28 benchmarks). `pnpm bench:compare` 0. `pnpm test:e2e` **37 passed in 44.7 s** on a loaded host.
- **`pnpm bench:browser` deferred, with numbers: the nineteenth consecutive cycle.** Load averages **96.13 / 98.48 / 72.89** at the first reading and **117.27 / 93.42 / 74.00** at the bench gate on 8 cores, so no fresh sample was taken and `docs/benchmarks.md` is unchanged. Two consequences stated plainly: `pnpm bench:compare` exiting 0 here re-gated the **archived** browser report of `2026-09-24T13:40:52Z` (`scripts/bench-compare.mjs` only reads `bench-results/browser-*.json`, and `pnpm bench` writes none), and two of its rows sit above their own max-of-five (`publish/dedicated` 41.33 vs 40.44, `publish/shared` 34.11 vs 33.99) without gating, because the gate requires *both* legs — the pct threshold (7.4%, 0.5%) and the ceiling. ## Phase 193 / 0.21.29 shipped: the tag run green, and the publication read carrying a failure mode none of the last twenty had

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.29` published. Material: Phase 192 (`#292`, branch `test/mutation-claim-recheck`, squash `1b90b37`; pre-squash `e0f7f1c` + `6d69df6` + `b068ee1` + `0a47b90` + `0efc332` + `a2ca8d6`) — four `docs(...)` commits over five `src/` files and one test header, the release prep, and the two `AGENTS.md` rules.
- **What the release carried.** No code. The IndexedDB settlement note's guard count went from four to five (four latch *variables*, five guarded closures — `load()`'s `oncomplete` shares its latch with that block's own `fail`); `CentrifugeSession`'s two dependency line citations became the dependency's own quoted comment text, after the recorded `build/index.js:762` was found to match **neither** the pinned 5.7.4 (763-764) nor the 5.7.0 copy in the store (748); the rotted `194/194` file count and the host-specific `~40 s` OOM timing were retired from all three copies that told that story; and two internal `:NNN` citations were replaced by the statements they named — those two still pointed roughly right, which is why they are the dangerous ones. See the `0.21.29` CHANGELOG section for each in full.
- **Publication evidence.** Release run `36057456454` on tag `v0.21.29` (tagging `1b90b37`) completed green in **6m36s** (20:49:30Z → 20:56:06Z, job `release`, **20/20** steps). `dist-tags.latest` on `registry.npmjs.org` reads **0.21.29**. `PUBLISHED_VERSION=0.21.29 pnpm verify:published` 0 on its **first** attempt ("verified published cross-tab-worker-databus@0.21.29 ESM/CJS consumers").
- **A new failure mode in the manual repeat: the registry read that returns the *previous* release.** The first two `npm view cross-tab-worker-databus version --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org` reads after this publish returned **0.21.28**; the same query for `versions dist-tags --json`, run between them, returned latest **0.21.29**, and a third read of the original form then agreed. So a bare `version` read can be served from npm's **local** cache, and naming `--registry` explicitly does not defeat that cache. This matters because `verify-published-consumer.mjs` falls back to exactly that read when `PUBLISHED_VERSION` is unset — so a hand-run `pnpm verify:published` minutes after a publish can exit 0 having verified the *last* release, and the only trace is the version in the line it prints. The tag workflow is immune (`release.yml` passes `PUBLISHED_VERSION: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}`), and `docs/release-checklist.md` already prescribes passing the version by hand, but for the propagation reason rather than this one; this repeat passed it explicitly, so the reading above is a hazard observed on this machine, not one that reached a verdict.
- **The number that survived in `main`'s log, and which artifact carried it.** `1b90b37`'s subject reads "twelve quoted measurements re-run", and twelve was a **tally of sites** from the branch's first draft — the class of claim this release exists to retire, and the reason it appears in no file: the CHANGELOG says so in its own header ("No total of runs is quoted here, because a total of runs is the same class of claim as the ones being audited"), and the roadmaps and Phase 192 name the sites instead. The title reached `main` through the **PR title**, which squash-merge composes the commit subject from, and it cannot be taken back: force-push and history rewrite are prohibited here, and the PR is closed. So this entry is the correction's home, and the accurate statement of what was re-run is Phase 192's site list plus the CHANGELOG's Fixed section — read those rather than the log line. A count that reaches `main` through a merge title is a new channel, and the one rule it yields is that the PR *title* is the last artifact to be scrubbed, not the first.
- **Which legs were deducted rather than deleted-and-counted.** `runTransport()`'s `status !== WORKER_STATUS.ERROR` survivor was **not** re-run this cycle, and the entry says so rather than letting the surrounding text imply a mutant that never happened. It follows from the row set re-derived one cycle earlier: the census at that line observes `1000`, `0000`, `0100`, `1001` and `1010` over the four premises in source order (`transportReady`, `status === ERROR`, `droppedAfterConnect`, `stopping`), and no row sets both bit 1 and bit 2 — which is exactly the condition the comment says the leg is held against. Deduction from a re-derived census is evidence; the two `reopenTransport` absorbs remain the cycle's acknowledged non-measurement, and their symmetric result dates from Phase 189.
- **Verification on the merged tree:** the tag's own tree — `git diff --stat a2ca8d6 1b90b37` is empty, so `pnpm check` 0 (936 tests / 37 files, 5/5 perf gates), `pnpm lint` 0, `pnpm test:coverage` 0 at 99.02 / 97.65 / 99.27 / 99.69 with the ledger at **46 zero-count arms of 1963**, `tests/documentation.test.ts` 18/18, `verify:compat` ("0.21.29 preserves public exports and type metadata from `v0.21.28`"), `verify:types` (6 entries, 90 importable names), `verify:pack`, `pnpm bench` and `pnpm bench:compare` all 0, and `pnpm test:e2e` 37 passed in 33.1 s were all taken against content identical to what shipped. `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.29 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` 0.
- **`pnpm bench:browser` deferred with numbers: the twenty-first consecutive cycle.** The three-load averages taken around this session's gate runs read 72.89 to 117.27 on 8 cores, so no fresh sample and `docs/benchmarks.md` unchanged; `bench:compare`'s green therefore still re-gates the archived 2026-09-24 browser report, the caveat recorded at the gate since Phase 190.
- **Branch and PR hygiene.** `#290`, `#291`, `#292` merged; `test/mutation-claim-recheck` and the record branch deleted with them. `git branch -r` now lists only `origin/main` and `origin/HEAD`, and `gh pr list --state open` is empty, so nothing is queued to collide at `docs/progress.md`'s anchor.
- **Risk / rollback:** comment-only. The squash commit `1b90b37` is the revert target; the published artifact is immutable, so a consumer-facing rollback is forward-only via `0.21.30`. No export, frame, option, default or storage key moved.
- **Next:** (1) `0.21.30` from the remaining claim queue, which is now partly worked: `cluster.ts`'s route-owner-cache eviction note said the cache is "at least one entry over the cap" at the eviction loop — measured at `routeOwnerCacheMax: 2`, a re-touch at the cap leaves `size` at 2 and drops nothing, so the inequality was backwards for every re-touch and for every fill below the cap; and `environment.ts`'s differential vector has been made rebuildable (26 writes, **23** distinct documents, because `1e999` is `Infinity` and `JSON.stringify` emits it as `null` — which is also why no non-finite `seq` can reach the `typeof` test). Still queued: `validation.ts`'s "six of those nine" fraction, `trace.ts`'s remaining measured legs, `data-bus.ts`'s two `reopenTransport` absorbs, and `cluster.ts`'s `knownTopics` claims beyond the two just checked. ## Phase 194 / 0.21.30 prepared: the claim queue's last sites, two false absolutes, and a release gate that could verify the wrong version

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.30` prepared, not yet tagged. Branch `docs/claim-batch-24`, cut from main at `1b90b37` and rebased onto `6bc46ab` (the `0.21.29` record). Commits: `f74a06f` (route-owner cache), `94c3f31` (envelope vector), `974caaa` (the six `37 test files`), `af6f76a` (publication gate + resolver tests), `d864830` + `5e4f877` (two `AGENTS.md` rules), `2a75d19` (validation vector + deletions), `1367d6f` + `323504f` (the two `data-bus` re-runs), then the release prep.
- **How the branch lost three commits, and how they came back.** `#293`'s record commit was made on its own branch, and the next three commits landed there too — the branch was never switched away from after `gh pr create`. `gh pr merge 293 --squash --delete-branch` then force-deleted that **local** branch, discarding the three commits that had never been pushed; they surfaced only because a later `git rebase` replayed 2 commits where 5 were expected. `git reflog` named the OIDs, `git show --stat` confirmed each one's content, and `git cherry-pick` restored all three onto the right branch. The rule that came out of it: the branch a PR was opened from is finished — switch to a fresh one before the next commit, and treat a commit-count mismatch after any rebase, checkout or branch deletion as an alarm rather than tidy bookkeeping.
- **Two absolutes the code refutes.** `touchRouteOwnerCache()`'s eviction loop said "the cache is at least one entry over the cap here, so the iterator always yields a key to drop"; measured at `routeOwnerCacheMax: 2` with two remote owners, filling to the cap and re-resolving either owner leaves `size` at 2 and the first iteration breaks without deleting — a call adds at most one *net* entry, so the cap is exceeded only when a new key arrives at a full cache. And six comments (five in `src/`, one in `tests/dedup-manager.test.ts`) said a deletion left "all 37 test files green", a count that adds nothing to "nothing fails" and goes false whenever a file is added; all six now say "the whole suite green".
- **Two differential vectors made rebuildable.** `validation.ts`'s "23-value vector (numeric strings, booleans, ±Infinity…)" became an explicit 25 inputs **including `3000`** — a differential where nothing is accepted proves nothing — and each guard as written vs with only its `typeof` operand deleted answered identically on all 25, same accept/reject and same message. `environment.ts`'s "23 stored values" became 26 writes / **23 distinct documents**, because `1e999` is `Infinity` and `JSON.stringify` emits `null`, so three rows store their `null` twin's bytes — which is also why no non-finite `seq` can reach the `typeof` test. The vectors still match for both deletions; `null` is the one input whose *exit route* parts (guard-rejected vs thrown-and-caught), and the note now says the vectors agree on delivery rather than implying they are identical everywhere.
- **The reopen absorb: four legs re-run, and the forcing had to be rebuilt.** The `51 tests fail` number had stood since the file held 194; at 198 the same 51 came back, and the other three legs reproduce green. The first construction replaced `pending` wholesale, and both legs that must be green then failed three tests each (`does not reopen a transport queued behind a pending stop when stop() is called`, `reopens after repeated hide/show cycles that all precede a pending initial open`, the async-stop recovery case) because those assert on *which* promise the reopen waits for. Appending the link to the real `startPromise ?? pendingStop` is the faithful forcing; a correct note would have been rewritten as stale on the first one's evidence. `AGENTS.md` gained both this rule and the fix to last cycle's own recipe: `diff | grep -c '^>'` reads 0 for a pure deletion, so three applied mutants were reported `VOID` — the counter belongs on `^[<>]`, and that failure biases toward surviving mutants, i.e. gaps that never existed.
- **The reopen gate's four operands: survivors, and tsc-clean too.** Each single-operand deletion at `runTransport()`'s gate left the whole suite green, as the note claimed. Newly measured: all four also pass `tsc --noEmit`, which separates this guard from the `?? fallback` legs elsewhere in the file that *only* the compiler holds — here neither stands between the deletion and a merge, and the comment says so.
- **A release gate that could pass while verifying the wrong artifact.** `verify-published-consumer.mjs` inferred its target from `npm view <pkg> version` when `PUBLISHED_VERSION` was unset; minutes after the 0.21.29 publish that read returned **0.21.28** twice while `versions dist-tags --json` on the same registry reported 0.21.29 and a third plain read agreed. Naming `--registry` does not defeat npm's local packument cache. The gate would download and import the previous artifact and exit 0, its version visible only in a line nothing forces anyone to read. An inferred version is now trusted only when it agrees with `package.json`, and an empty read is refused rather than becoming `pkg@` → `latest`. The `Release` workflow is immune (it passes the tag), so the exposure was the manual repeat the checklist prescribes. The body moved behind the sibling's `main()`/`invokedDirectly` gate so the resolver is a pure function with five tests, each mutation-checked: ignoring the explicit value dies to 2 tests, dropping the disagreement check to 1, dropping the empty check to 1 (it falls through to the other message), dropping the strip to 2.
- **Verification (this tree):** `pnpm check` 0, `pnpm lint` 0, `pnpm test:coverage` 0 with the ledger at **46 zero-count arms of 1963** and 99.02 / 97.65 / 99.27 / 99.69, `tests/documentation.test.ts` 18/18, `verify:compat` ("0.21.30 preserves public exports and type metadata from `v0.21.29`"), `verify:types` (6 entries, 90 importable names), `verify:pack`, `pnpm bench` and `pnpm bench:compare` all 0, `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.30 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` 0. Suite **941 tests / 37 files** — five new, all added to `tests/regression.test.ts` rather than a new file, because the file count is exactly the number this release retires from six comments.
- **`pnpm bench:browser` deferred, with numbers: the twenty-second consecutive cycle.** No idle window around this branch's gate runs, so `docs/benchmarks.md` is unchanged and `bench:compare`'s green still re-gates the archived 2026-09-24 browser report.
- **Risk / rollback:** the library is comment-only; the one behavioural change is in `scripts/verify-published-consumer.mjs`, which is not published in the package. Revert target is this PR's squash commit. Consumers are unaffected except that a hand-run `pnpm verify:published` without `PUBLISHED_VERSION` now fails when the registry read disagrees with `package.json` — pass the version explicitly to verify an older release.
- **Next:** (1) Tag and publish `0.21.30`, then record it. (2) The queue is nearly worked through; what remains, in descending expected yield: `trace.ts`'s remaining measured legs, and the `knownTopics` eviction claims beyond the FIFO/owned-guard/storage-less trio already confirmed against their tests in this pass. (3) The standing dependency patrol. (4) A `bench:browser` sample on a genuinely idle host — twenty-two cycles now, which means the gate's resolution on `publish/*` is still untested in this repository.

## Phase 195 / 0.21.30 shipped: the blocking gate failed on a good publish, and the note written about it an hour earlier was wrong too

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.30` published. PR #294 squash-merged as `035d458`, which is what `origin/main` points at and what the annotated tag `v0.21.30` resolves to. Release run `36062683927`: attempt 1 **failure**, attempt 2 — a re-run against the unchanged tag — **success**, job complete 21:47:14Z.
- **Publication evidence, five reads in clock order.** `npm publish` acked at 21:39:03Z. A `curl -s -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>` issued at 21:43:15Z reported `latest` still on 0.21.29, no `0.21.30` in `versions`, and no `time['0.21.30']`. npm's own stamp for that version is **21:44:12.987Z**, and the packument's `last-modified` is **21:44:14 GMT**. A `curl -I …/-/<pkg>-0.21.30.tgz` issued at 21:44:13Z returned `HTTP 200`, and a local `npm pack <pkg>@0.21.30 --registry https://registry.npmjs.org` issued at 21:44:34Z completed and wrote the tarball. `dist-tags.latest` is now 0.21.30, and attempt 2's step 15 — the same command with the same env the manual repeat uses — passed in 1 s.
- **What the gate did, and what it cost.** Attempt 1's `Verify published npm consumers` ran 21:39:03Z → 21:45:07Z, the entire 48 × 7.5 s budget, and died on `ETARGET: No matching version found for cross-tab-worker-databus@0.21.30` — while the tarball was already fetchable from this machine. Nothing was re-pushed and the tag was not moved; the re-run is the documented remedy for exactly this class of red.
- **A note of my own, retracted against its own timestamps.** `56ed7db`, committed less than an hour earlier on this same branch, explained those two disagreeing reads as "the document can lag the artifact… both statements were true of the same minute". The readings inside that paragraph contradict it: the 21:43:15Z stale-document read **preceded** the registry's own 21:44:12Z record, so nothing was lagging an existing artifact, and no `no-cache` request could have seen a version that did not exist yet. The genuine read-path disagreement is the *runner* still on `ETARGET` at 21:45:07Z after a HEAD and a pack from elsewhere had both succeeded by 21:44:35Z. Both language copies now carry the sequence with its clock readings, and say to probe from the machine that is failing, because "fetchable" is a per-machine answer.
- **The budget is a sum of two measured lags, not a comfort number.** `npm publish`'s ack precedes the registry's `time[<version>]` record by 74.8 s on 0.21.29, 96.8 s on 0.21.28, 248.7 s on 0.21.27 and 310.0 s on 0.21.30 (step completion vs packument stamp), and the packument is served `cache-control: public, max-age=300`, so a copy of it anywhere in the path may be a cache lifetime stale by design. That second term also explains a regularity that had been read as noise: three consecutive green tag runs consumed 305 s, 304 s and 304 s of the ceiling, in that order. `PUBLISHED_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS` goes 48 → 96, i.e. 720 s against a 610 s requirement.
- **The gate's floor moved from "5 minutes" to that requirement, and is mutation-checked.** `tests/workflows.test.ts` asserted `totalMs >= 5 * 60 * 1000`, which the 6-minute budget that had just failed a release satisfied — a floor that blessed the value under test. It now asserts `≥ packumentCacheLifetimeMs + maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs`. Measured: setting the workflow's attempts from 96 back to 48 fails exactly that test, with the message naming both lags (`expected 360000 to be greater than or equal to 610000`), and the file was restored byte-identical to `HEAD` afterwards. Evaluated against the same floor, both the 120 s budget 0.20.89 exhausted and the 360 s one that failed here are rejected.
- **Left open on purpose.** Which copy served the runner's stale views. A purely npm-local-cache account predicts attempt 2 should have waited for the same 300 s object lifetime, and it resolved in 1 s instead. The checklist and the workflow comment both record that as unsettled rather than naming a cache, and an untried remedy stays labelled untried: a revalidating request (`--prefer-online`) would answer it, but not by experimenting on a blocking gate.
- **Verification (this tree):** `pnpm check` 0 (37 test files, and the perf step green), `pnpm lint` 0, `git diff --check` clean, `tests/documentation.test.ts` 18/18 over the en/zh pair, `npx js-yaml` parses `release.yml`, and the budget arithmetic re-read *from the file*: attempts 96 × 7500 ms = 720 s, manual default 30 s, ratio 24×. No `src/` change in this cycle, so the arm ledger and the four coverage percentages stay 0.21.30's.
- **Risk / rollback:** the behavioural changes are a retry ceiling in `.github/workflows/release.yml` and its floor in `tests/workflows.test.ts`; neither is published inside the package, and both take effect on the next tag push. A too-long ceiling costs a later red on a genuinely missing package, which is the trade the measurement favours. Revert target is this branch's `fix(release): size the publish gate's budget from the two lags it must clear` commit.
- **Next:** (1) Finish `0.21.31` from this branch (`fix/wildcard-publish-cache`), whose other content is the uncapped-`wildcardPublishCache` record and three doc corrections, with its own prep entry. (2) Task #112 — an eviction rule for `wildcardPublishCache`, which needs a size test, the coordination sweep, and `pnpm bench` / `bench:compare`. (3) The standing dependency patrol. (4) A `bench:browser` sample on a genuinely idle host — twenty-two cycles now.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 196 / 0.21.31 prepared: a retry ceiling sized from two lags, a gate floor that the failing value had satisfied, and one load-dependent timeout

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.31` prepared, not yet tagged. Branch `fix/wildcard-publish-cache`, cut from `main` at `035d458` (the `0.21.30` squash commit). Commits: the route-owner/`wildcardPublishCache` record, `trace`'s kill-set names, the `architecture.md` en+zh cap paragraph, the checklist's publish-adjudication note, `fix(release): size the publish gate's budget from the two lags it must clear`, `docs(progress): record 0.21.30 as shipped…` (Phase 195), then this prep commit.

Deriving the number rather than raising it until things passed also accounted for a regularity three releases of logs had recorded as noise: the preceding green tag runs consumed 305 / 304 / 304 s of the ceiling, which is one cache lifetime plus command time.

It now asserts `packumentCacheLifetimeMs + maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs`, with the lookup for each term in the comment. Checked both ways: setting the workflow back to 48 fails exactly that test (`expected 360000 to be greater than or equal to 610000`, message naming both lags) and the file was restored byte-identical to `HEAD`; evaluated against the same floor, the 360 s budget that failed and the 120 s one 0.20.89 exhausted are both rejected.
- **The checklist note written during 0.21.30 was retracted against its own timestamps** (see Phase 195): its "both statements were true of the same minute" put a stale-document read at 21:43:15Z *before* the registry's 21:44:12Z record of that version. Both language copies now carry the ordered readings, state that absence from `versions`/`latest` minutes after a green publish step is the expected state of a success, and say to probe from the machine that is failing.
- **A `pnpm test:coverage` red traced to a per-file timeout rather than to the diff.** With the release tree otherwise green, `tests/version-compat.test.ts` died with `Error: Test timed out in 15000ms` (1 case on the coverage run, 2 on a second reading, different cases each time) while 940 of 941 passed. The mechanism is structural: every case there runs `git init/add/commit/tag` plus one `node` spawn, so the global 15 s applies to a cost that is five process starts, not an object comparison. Fixed with a per-file `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 60_000 })` rather than by loosening the global every in-process test relies on. Three readings, attributed: at load average 400+ with nothing of ours competing, one case crossed 15 s; the same file alone while a `pnpm bench` of ours ran on the machine reported 3–19 s for the survivors — that reading is confounded, and the comment says so; the same file alone with the contention gone ran all 18 in 23.7 s total. The override's binding was then falsified rather than trusted: with the value at `1`, 17 of 18 cases fail with `Test timed out in 1ms` and the run exits 1. Re-running the whole gate set afterwards on the same host (load still ~389) came back green, so the pin is demonstrated to clear this file's flake, not to make a slow file look fast.
- **`wildcardPublishCache`: the per-topic map the documented cap does not cover.** It was the only unbounded one among the maps beside it — one entry per distinct topic this worker publishes, cleared only on the two teardowns where its `clear()` sits beside a `routeOwnerCache.clear()` (verified by grepping both calls: exactly two such pairs in `cluster.ts`, and no other `wildcardPublishCache.clear()`). Measured: 1,200 `publish()` calls on distinct topic names leave `knownTopics` at its 500-entry cap and this map holding 1,200. The comment records why a cap is not free (evicting a pattern re-runs the first local dispatch; evicting a `null` re-scans and can hand a later publication the fan-out of a first one), which is what task #112 has to decide, and `docs/architecture.md` says the same in both languages. `trace.ts`'s flush-activity note also swapped its "(three cases… two cases…)" multiplicities for five verbatim test names, one of which records that `dispatched`'s pair spans two files.
- **Verification (this tree):** `pnpm check` 0, `pnpm lint` 0, `pnpm typecheck` 0, `pnpm test` 0 (**941 tests / 37 files** — no tests added this cycle), `pnpm test:coverage` 0 with the ledger unmoved at **46 zero-count arms of 1963** (re-derived from `coverage/coverage-final.json`) and 99.02 / 97.65 / 99.27 / 99.69, `tests/documentation.test.ts` 18/18, `verify:compat` ("0.21.31 preserves public exports and type metadata from `v0.21.30`"), `verify:types` (6 entries, 90 importable names, nothing dropped since `v0.21.30`), `verify:pack` (ESM/CJS root and subpath consumers from `cross-tab-worker-databus-0.21.31.tgz`), `pnpm bench`, `node scripts/bench-compare.mjs --fail-above-pct 50` → "no metric regressed more than 50%", `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.31 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` 0, `git diff --check` clean, and `npx js-yaml` parses the edited `release.yml`.
- **Deferred, with numbers.** `pnpm bench:browser`: the **twenty-third** consecutive cycle — every reading this session sat between load average 217 and 440 on 8 cores, and a loaded sample in the archive becomes the baseline the next release is judged against, which is the one outcome the standing decision exists to prevent. `pnpm test:e2e` was not run locally for the same reason (Playwright budgets are the first thing a 400-load host breaks); it is adjudicated by CI's `browser` job on this PR's commit instead, and the tag will not move until that job is green on the merged commit. `bench:compare`'s green therefore still re-gates the archived 2026-09-24 browser report, and note what it actually gates: the bare `pnpm bench:compare` runs with no `--fail-above-pct`, i.e. print-only, so the release record cites the `--fail-above-pct 50` invocation.
- **Risk / rollback:** no `src/` change, so consumers are unaffected. The behavioural edits are a retry ceiling in the `Release` workflow, a floor in `tests/workflows.test.ts`, and a per-file timeout in `tests/version-compat.test.ts` — none of them shipped inside the package. A too-long retry ceiling delays the red on a genuinely missing package from 6 to 12 minutes. Revert target is this PR's squash commit.
- **Next:** (1) Open the PR, wait for verify + browser, merge, tag `v0.21.31`, publish, verify, then record it. ## Phase 198 / 0.21.32 prepared: a publication that only the first send lost, and the memo that decided it

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.32` prepared, not yet tagged. Branch `release/0-21-32`, cut from `main` at `ba9400b` — PR #296's squash commit, merged 2026-09-24T22:59:13Z — whose library content is the reason for this release. This branch adds the `trace.ts` kill-set attribution, the `publish()` comment correction, the publication-lag prose from Phase 197, and the scratch-directory lint fix below.
- **The bug: a topic's first publication was addressed to the wrong worker, and only the first.** `publish()` and `publishBatch()` each carried a textually identical block that, while `wildcardPublishCache` held no entry for the topic, scanned the local wildcard patterns and — on a match — addressed the CONTROL frame to *this* worker without consulting the durable route. Every later publication for that topic did consult it. Measured with one runtime holding `chat.*` and a peer concretely owning `chat.room.1` (both `isAssigned` true, the route record naming the peer): three publications landed `1,0,0` on the sender and `0,1,1` on the owner. Delivery is at-most-once, so publication one is gone for good. The same shape reproduced for a two-item batch, whose frame the receiver unpacks per item.
- **Why the fix is a deletion rather than an eviction rule.** This is `0.20.58` from the other side — there a cached `null` short-circuited the owner lookup, here a cache *miss* did — and neither stored value decided anything: `pattern` and `null` were both read only as "have I scanned this topic yet". No rule about which half may be forgotten could have fixed the ordering, so the memo is gone and `resolvePublishTarget()` answers for every non-owned publication. Wildcard ownership is intact: with no live concrete route that call returns this worker, and the receiving gate matches the pattern. This also retires the unbounded growth `0.21.31` documented — it was a side effect of the fast path, so task #112's eviction question is not answered but dissolved.
- **`publish()`'s own comment was the last survivor of the removed mechanism, and it was false.** Above the `assignedTopics.has(topicKey)` early return it still read "Wildcard assignments also own matching concrete topics, so they can use the same fast path". With the memo gone that sentence describes nothing, and it was never true of *that* lookup: `assignedTopics` is keyed by the plaintext it was handed, so a `chat.*` holder carries the *pattern's* key and `has(concreteKey)` misses — which is exactly why the fix works. Verified against `isAssigned()`, which needs its own `topicMatchesPattern` loop to say what the comment implied `has()` could do. The sentence now names which lookup answers for which assignment. `publishBatch()` carried no such sentence, and its `has()` block is checked against the same claim.
- **Pinned one publication at a time.** `forwards a topic's FIRST publish to its concrete remote owner, not to a matching local wildcard` and `forwards a batch's FIRST publish to the concrete remote owner as well` each assert on a single send, so a regression names *which* publication was lost rather than reporting a count short by one. Without the fix they fail at `expected +0 to be 1` and `expected [] to deeply equal [1, 2]`; with it the file is green. Three older cases that named the removed cache in their titles were retitled to what they assert, and the single-runtime pair among them marked characterization — a lone runtime always wins its own election, so it cannot distinguish the two paths.
- **Re-measured on this tree rather than carried forward.** All four single-operand deletions of `trace.ts`'s flush-activity guard, run one at a time against the 943-test suite: `received` reddens 3, `dispatched` 2, `dedupAccepted` 1, `dedupSuppressed` 1 — each `applied=1`, each restore `byte-identical`, and the failing test's file printed per mutant. The comment now names that file for every kill, because `dispatched`'s two sit in two different files (`tests/data-bus.test.ts`, `tests/trace.test.ts`) and the previous "(two cases)" hid it.
- **A scratch directory inside the linted tree turned `pnpm lint` red with errors that named no product code.** The probe harness lived in `.gate-logs/` — in-tree by design, because `/tmp` evicted a failing log mid-session earlier and `pnpm test:coverage` deletes `coverage/`, which is where logs had also been written. `eslint .` picked the harness up and reported 9 errors (`no-undef` on `console`/`process`, `no-control-regex`), which reads as a lint failure of the release tree. Fixed at both ends: `.gate-logs/` in `.gitignore` with the reason written beside it, and `.gate-logs/**` in the eslint ignores. `tests/regression.test.ts`'s "keeps scripts/ covered by ESLint" still passes, so the release tooling stays linted — the ignore is scoped to scratch, not to a directory that ships.
- **What `bench:compare`'s green does and does not say, re-read rather than inherited.** `scripts/bench-compare.mjs` filters the archive to `browser-*.json` (its own header: "Compare archived browser benchmark reports"), and `pnpm bench` is `vitest bench --run`, which writes nothing into `bench-results/`. So this cycle's pair re-gated `browser-2026-09-24T13-40-52-413Z.json` against the median of the five browser reports before it — both taken **before** 0.21.29 published — and therefore says nothing about this tree. It also explains a row that would otherwise read as an alarm beside a publish-path fix: `publish/dedicated/perMessageMs 38.471 -> 41.3311 (+7.4%)` is one archived browser sample against five older ones, not 0.21.32's code. The perf assertion that *did* cover this change is `pnpm test:perf`, 5/5 green. `pnpm bench` also ran to completion, but it asserts nothing on its own — it is a crash check plus the report the compare step reads — so between the two, no gate measured this release's publish path against its baseline. The browser sample stays deferred (twenty-fourth cycle), and this release is the one that would have benefited from taking it.
- **Verification (this tree, all thirteen steps exit 0):** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (**37 files / 943 tests**), `pnpm test:perf` (5/5), `pnpm test:coverage` (0, with the ledger re-derived from `coverage/coverage-final.json` as **46 zero-count arms of 1951** at **99.02 / 97.64 / 99.27 / 99.69**), `verify:compat` ("0.21.32 preserves public exports and type metadata from v0.21.31"), `verify:types` ("6 entries, 90 importable names, surface closed, nothing dropped since v0.21.31"), `verify:pack` (ESM/CJS root and subpath consumers from `cross-tab-worker-databus-0.21.32.tgz`), `pnpm bench`, `bench-compare --fail-above-pct 50`, `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.32 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs`, `git diff --check`. The set ran twice: once before the `publish()` comment landed, which is where lint's 9 scratch-dir errors appeared, and once after every edit, which is the list above. Host load averaged 125 falling to 55 across the run on 8 cores.
- **Ledger movement, stated as the ratio it is.** The zero-arm count held at **46** while the denominator fell from 1963 to **1951**, because deleting the memo removed twelve branch slots with it — which is why the branch aggregate moved 97.65 → 97.64 with no new verdict owed and none closed.
- **Deferred, with numbers.** `pnpm bench:browser`: twenty-fourth consecutive cycle (see the `bench:compare` bullet above for what that costs this release in particular). `pnpm test:e2e` not run locally, adjudicated by CI's `browser` job on this PR's commit; the tag does not move until that job is green on the merged commit.
- **Risk / rollback:** the behavioural change is one routing decision inside `publish()`/`publishBatch()`, both reached only from a worker that holds a matching wildcard while a *different* worker holds the concrete route. A consumer that depended on the old behaviour depended on a lost publication. The public surface is unchanged and the removed field was private. Revert target is `ba9400b`, shipped as a new patch version rather than a moved tag.
- **Next:** (1) Open the PR, wait for verify + browser, merge, tag `v0.21.32`, publish, verify, record. (2) The standing dependency patrol, re-run against the registry rather than `pnpm outdated` (which retried `react` three times against an unreachable mirror and returned a single row): everything current except `typescript` 6.0.3 → 7.0.2, still blocked upstream — `typescript-eslint` 8.70.1 *and* its canary 8.70.2-alpha.7 both declare `typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0`. Take the canary from `dist-tags.canary`: sorting version strings puts `8.9.1-alpha.9` last, because `9` sorts after `70`, and the line to watch is 8.70.x. Both roadmap copies now say that, and their two disagreeing check dates (09-23 / 09-22) became one. (3) A `bench:browser` sample on a genuinely idle host, which this release makes more overdue than usual.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 199 / 0.21.32 shipped: the first behaviour change since 0.21.25, and a publication sample that fits the cache model to the second

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.32` published. PR #297 squash-merged as `a372980` (merged 2026-09-24T23:31:54Z); annotated tag `v0.21.32` points at that commit and was pushed with the HTTP/1.1 + large-post-buffer form the checklist prescribes. Release run `36073312261`: **attempt 1, success**, job 23:33:23Z → 23:39:53Z, every step green. `npm view cross-tab-worker-databus dist-tags` now reads `latest: 0.21.32`.
- **Publication evidence, step by step.** Step 13 `Create GitHub release` 23:34:12Z → 23:34:13Z. Step 14 `Publish to npm` 23:34:13Z → **23:34:46Z** (33 s). Step 15 `Verify published npm consumers` 23:34:46Z → **23:39:50Z** = **304 s**, green on the first attempt, i.e. 42% of the 720 s ceiling. The registry's own `time['0.21.32']` is **23:36:02.091Z** — **76.1 s** after the ack, the second-smallest of the six samples now listed (74.8 / 96.8 / 127.2 / 248.7 / 310.0 s plus this one), so **the 310 s maximum that sizes the ceiling is unchanged** and `maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs` stays put.
- **What this release adds to the open question, and it is a lot.** The record existed 76 s in; a `curl -H "Cache-Control: no-cache"` packument read from this machine saw `latest = 0.21.32` at 23:37:17Z, 151 s in; and the runner still took **304 s** — which is one 300 s cache lifetime plus ~4 s of command time, measured from the runner's own first fetch at the step's opening. Seven green samples now sit at 304–308 s, and this one lands inside a single 7.5 s poll interval of the model's prediction. That is the cleanest support the lifetime account has, and it also disqualifies a sentence I wrote last cycle: the checklist cites 0.21.30's "retry resolved before a fresh 21:44 fetch's 300 s lifetime had run out" as an observation *against* a purely local account, but the two events it joins are from different machines — the fresh read was this laptop's `npm pack` at 21:44:34Z, while the 1 s green was a **new runner job** whose cache starts empty, which the local model predicts rather than contradicts. What a purely-local-cache account still cannot explain is one specific reading: the runner's `ETARGET` at **21:45:07Z**, 364 s after that step opened its first poll at 21:39:03Z and so ~60 s *after* a copy taken at that moment must have expired. Filed as task #117 to correct both language copies and every restatement, rather than left standing in prose consumers read.
- **What this release is, in one line.** The first change to library *behaviour* since `0.21.25`: a topic's first publication from a worker holding a matching wildcard was addressed to itself without consulting the durable route, so with one runtime on `chat.*` and a peer concretely owning `chat.room.1` three publications delivered `1,0,0`/`0,1,1` and the first was lost under at-most-once delivery. The memo that decided it is deleted rather than bounded, because neither of its two value shapes ever decided anything — `0.20.58` from the other side, a cache *miss* where that one was a cache hit. Both pinning tests were re-run individually on the merged tree and pass with the names the CHANGELOG quotes verbatim.
- **Gate set, run twice on this content.** All thirteen steps exit 0: `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, `test` (37 files / **943 tests**), `test:perf` (5/5), `test:coverage` (ledger re-derived at **46 zero-count arms of 1951**, 99.02 / 97.64 / 99.27 / 99.69 — the zero count held while the denominator fell by 12, because deleting the memo deleted its branches), `verify:compat`, `verify:types` (6 entries / 90 names), `verify:pack`, `bench`, `bench-compare --fail-above-pct 50`, `verify-release-version`, `git diff --check`. CI on the PR before merge: `verify` 2m9s, `browser` 2m24s, `analyze` 1m18s, CodeQL pass.
- **The `bench:compare` limit found while writing the record, stated where it will be read.** `scripts/bench-compare.mjs` filters `bench-results/` to `browser-*.json`, and `pnpm bench` (`vitest bench --run`) writes nothing there — so its green re-gated `browser-2026-09-24T13-40-52-413Z.json`, a sample taken *before* 0.21.29 published. It also explains a row that reads as an alarm next to a publish-path fix: `publish/dedicated/perMessageMs 38.471 → 41.3311 (+7.4%)` is one old browser sample against five older ones, not this code. Recorded in Phase 198 and in the CHANGELOG of the release it first confused. The consequence for the standing decision: `bench:browser` is now twenty-four cycles deferred, and this release is the one where that cost actual coverage, since `test:perf` is the only perf gate that saw the change.
- **Three shipped-comment enumerations re-checked, all three accurate** (the reverse of a finding, recorded so the next pass does not re-derive them): `data-bus.ts`'s "`pendingStop` is written in exactly four places" and "`transportReady = false` … exactly five" match their `grep -n` sites, with the two non-null installs of `pendingStop` correctly separated from the two `= null`; `data-bus.ts`'s "four sites that install a promise" for `startPromise` is exactly the four non-null assignments (`start()`, both `suspendTransport()` branches, `reopenTransport()`) out of ten statements touching the field; and `cluster.ts`'s "of the four callers, two re-test `started` locally" holds for `reconcile()` at 429/433/1000/1050, including which two. `version.ts`'s "only one of them evaluates this expression" looked false until its own header was read — "the two readers of *this file* at source level" are `vitest.config.ts` and `pnpm typecheck`, not the two `SDK_VERSION` read sites, and under that definition the clause is exact.

## Phase 200 / 0.21.33 prepared: a counter-observation that joined two machines, and the sample that showed it

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.33` prepared, not yet tagged. Branch `docs/record-0-21-32-shipped`, cut from `main` at `a372980` (the `0.21.32` squash commit). Commits on it: the Phase 199 shipped record, `docs(release): retract a counter-observation that joined two machines`, then this prep commit. No `src/` change; the release is docs, one workflow comment and one test comment.
- **What was wrong.** `docs/release-checklist.md` (both languages), `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s comment at the blocking step, and `AGENTS.md`'s restatement all supported "which copy served the stale views is not established" with an *argument*: that a purely-local npm cache account was refuted because "the retry resolved before a fresh 21:44 fetch's 300 s lifetime had run out". Two readings, two hosts. The 21:44:34Z fresh read was a `npm pack` on this laptop; the 1 s green at 21:47:10Z was a **new runner job**, and a new job's npm cache starts empty. A new process reading fresh at 487 s after an ack is what the local model predicts, so the pair was never a refutation, and the sentence was load-bearing for a verdict consumers act on when a release goes red.
- **What remains unexplained, stated as the one reading it is.** A purely-local account cannot explain the runner's own `ETARGET` at 21:45:07Z: the poll loop opened at 21:39:03Z, so that failure came 364 s later — roughly 60 s *after* a copy fetched at the loop's start must have expired under `max-age=300`. The text now names that as the surviving anomaly and keeps the verdict *not established*, which is a stronger position than the previous one: the conclusion is unchanged, and the reason for it is now a single measurement rather than a cross-machine comparison.
- **`0.21.32` arrived mid-cycle and is the model's cleanest support.** Ack 23:34:46Z (step 14 completion), registry `time['0.21.32']` 23:36:02.091Z = **76.1 s**, a `curl -H "Cache-Control: no-cache"` packument read from this machine reporting `latest = 0.21.32` at 23:37:17Z (151 s in), and step 15 green at 23:39:50Z = **304 s** — one 300 s lifetime plus a few seconds of command time, measured from the runner's own first fetch, and inside a single 7.5 s poll interval of the prediction. The verify-duration series is now seven green samples at 304–308 s (307/304/305/304/304 under the old ceiling; 308 under the raised one, then 304); the ack→record series is 248.7 / 96.8 / 74.8 / 310.0 / 127.2 / 76.1 s.
- **The constant deliberately did not move, and that is checked rather than asserted.** 76.1 s does not beat the 310 s maximum that sizes the 720 s budget, so `maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs` stays at `310_000` and `tests/workflows.test.ts` passes **6/6 with no edit to its assertions** — widening both lists while the derivation stands is the outcome that says the ceiling is sized right, and a future sample that *does* exceed 310 s is what should raise it, which is the rule the checklist now states with the lookup attached.
- **History was corrected by pointer, not by rewrite.** `CHANGELOG.md`'s `0.21.31` bullet and both `docs/roadmap.md` copies keep the sentence they got wrong and add a parenthetical naming `0.21.33` as what supersedes it. Rewriting released notes would erase the fact that the error shipped, which is the part a later reader needs in order to distrust the right thing; the grep used to find the copies was for the *vocabulary of the mechanism* (`argues against` / `反对纯本地` / `purely-local` / `等满 300`), not for a phrase, because the four copies paraphrase each other.
- **Verification (this tree, thirteen steps, every one exit 0):** `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, `test` (37 files / **943 tests**), `test:perf` (5/5), `test:coverage`, `verify:compat` ("0.21.33 preserves public exports and type metadata from `v0.21.32`"), `verify:types` ("6 entries, 90 importable names, surface closed and nothing dropped since `v0.21.32`"), `verify:pack`, `bench`, `bench-compare --fail-above-pct 50` ("no metric regressed more than 50%"), `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.33 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs`, `git diff --check`. **The ledger re-derived identical to `0.21.32`'s — 46 zero-count arms of 1951 at 99.02 / 97.64 / 99.27 / 99.69** — which is the control that makes "no `src/` change" a measurement rather than a description: the same script that produced last cycle's numbers produced these, on a tree whose only source-level difference is two comments. `tests/workflows.test.ts` 6/6 with its assertions untouched. Host load averaged 264 across the run on 8 cores, which is why the load-dependent `bench:compare` note below is not read as a regression signal.
- **Two more findings queued rather than folded in, with their evidence.** Task #116: `src/core/hash.ts` still asserts primality at line 26 ("distinct large primes") and lines 70-71 ("a shift and prime … also shifted and primed") after `0.21.29` corrected exactly that claim for the four per-character multipliers — factored today, `AVALANCHE_PRIME` = 15809 × 142123 and `AVALANCHE_CROSS` = 1223 × 2670883, both composite and both odd, and the `docs/progress.md` line for that pass says the comment "now says so" for the avalanche pair, which it does not. Task #118: `docs/roadmap.md` carries **143** `## <version> delivered scope` headings against **142** in the Chinese mirror, and the set difference is exactly `0.20.68` — the mirror has every neighbour and runs down to 0.11.0, so it is an omission, not a boundary; `tests/documentation.test.ts` passed across it, which is the part worth fixing with a heading-**set** comparison in both directions rather than a bullet count.
- **Risk / rollback:** no `src/` change, so consumers' runtime behaviour is untouched; the shipped surface is the two doc mirrors and `AGENTS.md`'s rule text. `PUBLISHED_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS` stays 96 and the workflow's arithmetic is unchanged — only its comment differs. Revert target is this PR's squash commit; nothing published moves.
- **Next:** (1) Open the PR, wait for verify + browser, merge, tag `v0.21.33`, publish, verify, record. (2) task #116 — the two surviving `prime` claims in `src/core/hash.ts` (lines 26 and 70-71) and the `docs/progress.md` line that over-claimed the earlier fix. (3) task #118 — the `0.20.68` mirror gap and the heading-set parity test that would have caught it. (4) A `bench:browser` sample on a genuinely idle host — twenty-fifth cycle; this cycle's readings reached 264 on 8 cores. (5) The standing dependency patrol: unchanged, `typescript` 6.0.3 → 7.0.2 blocked by `typescript-eslint`'s `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0` on latest *and* canary.

## Phase 201 / 0.21.33 corrected before its tag: three numbers that named the wrong quantity, and a release record with 41 unpublished versions

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.33`, prepared at `049ad8a` (PR #298, squash-merged; CI green on exactly that tree — `verify` 2m7s, `browser` 2m25s, `analyze` 1m9s, CodeQL pass, and the merged commit's tree hash is byte-identical to the PR head's `6d8cea9`, so CI's green covers the tag commit's content). **Not tagged yet**: re-reading the release prose against the run records turned up three numbers that each named a different quantity than the sentence claimed, and all three reach consumers through `CHANGELOG.md` — which ships inside the tarball and becomes the GitHub release notes — so they were corrected before the tag rather than retracted after it. - **(3) A retired draft still standing in the log.** `docs/progress.md` line 8812 still carried "about 5 min 40 s after the fetch that should have gone stale by 21:44:05Z" — a number that matches neither the 364 s span nor the ~60 s past-expiry every other copy states, and the one surviving copy of a sentence Phase 200 corrected elsewhere. - **A fourth candidate that was not a defect, checked before "fixing" it.** `docs/progress.md` says the laptop's fresh read was at **21:44:34Z** while the workflow comment says **21:44:35Z**, which reads as a copy that drifted. It is not one: the first is the `npm pack` "fresh fetch" in the retraction sentence, the second is the closing of the `curl -I` HEAD / local-pack window in the paragraph after it — two events, two timestamps, consistent in both languages. Writing an "alignment" edit here would have destroyed a correct reading, and the only way to see that was to read what each timestamp was attached to rather than to diff the strings.
- **What checking (1) turned up, and it is bigger than (1).** To settle the list's size, the two releases below its stated range were sampled the way the prose says to (`gh api` step completion minus the packument's `time[<version>]`): **0.21.25 is 157.8 s** (ack 17:56:53Z, record 17:59:30.781Z) and 0.21.26 is **96.1 s** (ack 18:41:40Z, record 18:43:16.084Z). Their verify steps come back at 307 s and 304 s — exactly the two durations already on file for those runs — so the run↔version attribution is confirmed by a number that predates this commit, which is the part of the measurement worth trusting. Eight gaps now exist; none beats 310.0 s, so `maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs`, the 720 s ceiling and the shipped lists' declared range are unchanged, and the two new values were recorded here and in the changelog/roadmap rather than pasted into every restatement. Filed as task #121 with the fix that fits the current chain — a check inside `scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` (the step that already talks to the registry at tag time) that no other CHANGELOG section is missing from npm, plus a convention note for the historical hole rather than 41 rewritten sections.

- **Milestone / version:** no release from this branch — its content is `0.21.34` material (one comment-only `src/` file, two docs, one test, `AGENTS.md`). Commits, by subject because a rebase rewrites OIDs: `docs(hash): the multipliers are odd, not prime…`, `docs(roadmap): move the 0.20.68 block into the ledger's own order…`, `docs(progress): mark the log line that read its own fix as covering all six…`, plus the two `AGENTS.md` rules and this entry.
- **Task #116, closed.** Two comments in `src/core/hash.ts` called the mixing constants primes. Factored by trial division on this tree: `PRIME_H1/H3/H4` are prime, `PRIME_H2 = 929 × 1_719_413`, and the avalanche pair is composite too — `AVALANCHE_PRIME = 15809 × 142123`, `AVALANCHE_CROSS = 1223 × 2_670_883` — with all six odd, which is the property that makes a `Math.imul` multiply a bijection on 32 bits. The values are untouched (a "correction" to a prime would re-cluster every route and worker key already in localStorage); the notes now carry the factorizations and say what the property actually is. Also re-checked while in the file: four distinct 32-bit seeds, four lanes, the 16/13 shift pair, and a 4 × 8-hex digest = the documented 128-bit key.
- **Task #118, closed with its premise retracted.** It was filed as "the Chinese roadmap lacks its `0.20.68` delivered-scope block". It does not: the block exists, titled `## 0.20.68 已交付` where the other 141 zh blocks say `已完成范围`, and the heading-set diff that reported the absence was keyed on that suffix — a paraphrase read as a missing section. What measurement did find, in both languages: of 144 release-scope blocks exactly one sat outside the section's descending order (`0.20.68`, after `0.11.0`, where an appended block had landed). So the zh heading now uses the convention, and both blocks moved to the position the ledger's own rule puts them — 4 lines out, 4 lines in, bullet text preserved verbatim in each language.
- **The gate, and what each leg was written against.** `tests/documentation.test.ts` gains one test with three assertions: allowed title set per file, strictly descending order of scope blocks, and an identical version set across the two languages. Mutation-checked one at a time, each restore byte-identical: reintroducing the `已交付` title fails **1** test with the message quoting the offending heading and the allowed set; relocating the en block back below `0.11.0` fails **1** — the pure move breaks only the new gate, because `## ` counts and list-item counts are untouched, which is exactly the blind spot; deleting the zh block fails **3** (the new mirror leg naming `0.20.68`, plus the two pre-existing equal-count gates). The third leg is prospective — measured clean across all ten localized doc pairs today — and the first two are not.
- **Two instrument failures worth recording, both caught before they became findings.** The first descending-order scan I wrote reported **143** violations on a file where the correct answer is 1, because it tested `if (a-b)` (any difference) instead of `if (a-b) <= 0` (wrong direction): an instrument whose "did it detect" check is inverted reports the whole series as a defect, and the only reason I noticed is that I already knew the answer. The second was an `AGENTS.md` edit whose replacement silently dropped the neighbouring Centrifuge bullet — visible immediately as `git diff --numstat` saying 2/1 where a pure insertion must say 3/0 — restored from `git show HEAD:AGENTS.md`, re-verified at 108 bullets with the diff back to a clean 2/0. Same rule as a scripted file rewrite: check the shape of the diff before believing the edit.
- **Verification (this tree, twelve steps, every one exit 0):** `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, `test` (37 files / **944 tests** — the +1 is the new gate), `test:perf` (5/5), `test:coverage` (37 / 944; aggregates 99.02 / 97.64 / 99.27 / 99.69 and the ledger re-derived at **46 zero-count arms of 1951**, identical to `0.21.33`, which is the control that a comment-only `src/` edit moved nothing), `verify:compat`, `verify:types`, `verify:pack`, `bench`, `bench-compare --fail-above-pct 50`, `git diff --check`. Full log: `.gate-logs/gate-hash-roadmap.log`. `verify-release-version.mjs` is not run here — it is a tag-time step, and it exits 1 without `RELEASE_TAG` by design.
