## Phase 204 / a census total that measured the runner: `stop()`'s 626-of-7589 re-derived as 782-of-20521, and the decay rule's own example had decayed

- **Milestone / version:** no release. Comment and instruction text only, on `docs/re-derive-stop-census` cut from `main` at `328dff0` (0.21.33). `git diff -U0 src/` was filtered for any added or removed line not beginning with `//` and returned nothing, so the emitted surface is untouched — and the ledger was then **re-derived on the changed tree instead of inferred from that filter**: `coverage/coverage-final.json` reports 46 zero-count branch arms of 1951 with the identical per-file split (cluster 13, data-bus 11, replay-persistence 6, replay-manager 5, trace 3, port-reaper 3, websocket 2, one each in centrifuge-session, centrifuge and version) and the same four numbers 99.02 / 97.64 / 99.27 / 99.69; `git diff --name-only` lists `src/core/data-bus.ts`, `src/core/trace.ts`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/progress.md`.
- **Three counts had rotted, and one of them stood inside the rule that warns about rotting counts.** Re-running the flag-vector census that produced the 0.21.23 operand verdicts: the `stop()` early-return guard is evaluated **20521** times over one whole-suite run and **782** of those read `(0,0,0,0)`, where the site comment claimed 626 of 7589. The same 7589 was quoted in `AGENTS.md`'s bullet about decaying counts, in this file's Phase 178 entry, and in both roadmap languages. `src/core/trace.ts`'s sink-default note claimed "the 884-test suite is green either way" — the deletion was re-run and **944** tests pass, so the verdict survives and only its denominator had decayed.
- **Why the total moved 2.7× while the suite grew 7% is the finding, not the drift.** 18130 of the 20521 evaluations come from `tests/coordination-invariants.test.ts`, measured by running that file alone under the probe; then the attribution was falsified in the other direction, by temporarily setting that file's `MAX_SEEDS` to 1,000 — same file, 3648 evaluations and 36 all-false rows against 205 at 5,000. A fuzz-weighted census total is therefore a property of the sweep depth and the host, not of the guard, which makes the old figure unreconstructable rather than merely outdated. Both sites now carry the lookup and the row provenance instead of a bare number.
- **What survived, named so nobody re-digs it.** Seven distinct rows ✓; `(0,0,1,0)` at 4 ✓ (the one pinned `pendingStop` premise); the recovery-timer guard's 2 premise rows and its 47 no-early-return rows ✓, with one precision added — the callback executes **50** times and one of those is absorbed by the `timerToken` check, so "forty-nine callback executions" counted guard-reaching evaluations while reading as a total — and the companion claim (those counts contain no fuzz volume) measured rather than inferred, by running the same probe against `tests/coordination-invariants.test.ts` alone and recording no callback at all. `tests/data-bus.test.ts` still holds 198 tests ✓, `tests/property.test.ts` still builds a no-arg reporter exactly 300 times (200 + 100 loop iterations, the third loop in that file builds none) ✓, and `validation.ts`'s differential vector does name 25 values ✓. The numeric-adjective sweep over `src/` came back clean at every site, so these are recorded rather than re-derived — each with the `this.`-prefixed lookup that returns its own number, since the bare field name also matches reads, writes and comment mentions: `confirmRoute()` has exactly three call sites (`grep -c "this.confirmRoute(" src/core/cluster.ts`), `connectPromise` is assigned in exactly two statements (`grep -c "this.connectPromise =" src/websocket.ts`), `metricsActive` has exactly seven readers (`grep -c "this.metricsActive" src/core/trace.ts`) and the `stopped` behind it is *read* in exactly two places — the getter's own term and `event()`'s guard — with the other three `this.stopped` hits in that file being two writes and one comment, so the grep's total is five and the reads are not (`grep -n "this\.stopped" src/core/trace.ts`), `transportReady` is set false at exactly the five sites its enumeration names and set true at exactly one (`grep -c "this.transportReady = false"`, `grep -c "this.transportReady = true"`), `pendingStop` is written in four places and assigned **non-null** in exactly two of them (`grep -c "this.pendingStop ="`, the other two writes being `null`), and `CentrifugeSession.subscribe()` wires exactly the three events its comment counts (`publication`, `error`, `unsubscribed`). One self-inflicted finding worth keeping: the first draft of this sentence "corrected" that method name to `handle()`, because the scan used to find the enclosing method matched only two-space-indented declarations and so skipped `private subscribe()` at 154 — refuted by `grep -n "subscribe(" src/centrifuge-session.ts`, which is the lesson, and a reminder that a correction derived from a shape-based scan is a claim, not evidence. and the websocket timer guard's "all three terms" is its actual term count (`this.socket !== socket || this.handlers !== handlers || handshakeCompleted`). No line number is written down here, because that is the class of citation this repository has already had to retire twice.
- **The sibling census held, and its "only" claim was upgraded from a first sight to an enumeration.** `runTransport()`'s four-premise guard was probed the same way: the row set came back as exactly the five the comment lists (`1000` 15120, `0000` 6231, `1001` 2520, `0100` 3, `1010` 2 out of 23876 evaluations — counts written here and not at the site, because 20173 of those 23876 come from the coordination fuzz, measured by running that file alone under the same probe, so the total belongs to the runner), and the note's sentence "the only thing in the suite that reaches" the `1001` row had been supported only by a *first-sight* stack, which can name a path but cannot exclude another. Capturing the stack at every one of the 2520 evaluations returned **one distinct signature** (`beginStop()` → `stop()` → `pause()` → `handoffAssignedTopics()` → `onControl()` → `unsubscribeTransport()`), so the word "only" now rests on a count rather than on an accident of ordering. `AGENTS.md` gained that rule, because the site's own phrasing was the kind a later reader would trust.
- **A larger defect than the arithmetic, surfaced by the same numbers.** The retired sentence read "why this return is **the common case**: 626 of the 7589". That share was 8% then and 3.8% now; the case that is actually common by count is `1001` (18024, 88%) — a live bus being stopped. The number never supported the word in either tree. Rewritten as "routine, not exotic", which is what 782 absolute evaluations establish and no ratio is needed for.
- **The verdict this phase was sent to check, and it held.** `src/workers/port-reaper.ts`'s `schedule()` arm claim — `remove()`/`setTimeout()` behind `targets.has(port)` (lines 114, 100), the reap pass re-arming only `if (reapedAny)` (239), and `dispose()` having no Worker-side caller "recorded in configuration.md" — re-read against source and docs: the SharedWorker entry calls only `register`/`touch`/`remove`/`setTimeout`, and `docs/configuration.md:219` with `docs/zh/configuration.md:212` both carry the `dispose()` sentence. No change shipped for it.
- **A dependency-citation pass, and the defect it found was in this repository's prose, not the SDK.** The comment that names `centrifuge@5.7.4` was re-read against the installed package: `getToken` really is at `build/types.d.ts:126`, the no-op guard really is at `build/index.js:763-764`, `BaseSubscription`'s class body really is 667-2673, and the twelve `emit('error')` sites count exactly inside that range. What was wrong is *which class installs the listener*: the text said "the `Subscription` constructor installs its own no-op `error` listener", and `Subscription`'s body contains **zero** `on('error')` calls — the guard runs in the `BaseSubscription` constructor every subscription reaches through `super`. A verifier sent to the named class finds no code there, which is the paraphrase hazard one level down. Both copies corrected.
- **The restatement grep then found a duplication defect in `AGENTS.md`.** Grepping the corrected claim's vocabulary turned the paragraph up **twice**: bullet 266 ("A count is a claim about one set…") carried 1595 characters of bullet 267's body verbatim after its own. Neither bullet's rule contradicted the other, which is why nobody had noticed — a reader of 266 gets a complete-looking paragraph that belongs to its neighbour, and a future correction of that paragraph would have to be made twice. 266 was truncated at the junction by an asserted single-line script (line count unchanged at 352, bullet count 109, the marker string now found once), and `CHANGELOG.md`'s copy of the sentence under `## [0.21.13]` is left standing for the reason above: a published section is a dated record.
- **Verification:** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (37 files / 944 tests), `pnpm lint` all green on the final tree, log at `.gate-logs/gate-phase204.log`; `pnpm test:perf`, `pnpm test:coverage` and the three `verify:*` gates are left to CI's `verify` job, which runs the whole of `pnpm check` on the same content — the local host read load 25 on 8 cores at phase start, and absolute-ms perf gates are the class of check that measurement exists to keep off a loaded core. Probe logs: `.gate-logs/census-run-{1..6}.log`, `census-depth1000.log`, `trace-sink-mutant.log`, `stop-census-run{1..4}.txt`. Every probe went onto a committed tree and came off with `git checkout -- <file>`; the one `tests/` excursion (`MAX_SEEDS`) was reverted by targeted edit and confirmed byte-identical with `git diff --stat` before the final run, and the sentence in this entry that first said "byte-identical across five runs" was corrected to "both runs that recorded it", because the recovery probe was measured twice, not five times.
- **Blockers:** none. **Risk / rollback:** text only, no tag and no publication involved. Published `CHANGELOG.md` sections that quote 7589 are deliberately left standing — a release note is a dated record of what was measured at that release, so correcting it would falsify history rather than correct a claim; the living instruction in `AGENTS.md` is what changed, and it now says which side of a release a tally was taken on.
- **Next:** (1) PR this branch and merge. (2) `feat/changelog-registry-completeness-gate` (task #121) rebases onto the new `main` and takes the following Phase number — the anchor rule means it can be pushed only once this is merged. (3) the standing `bench:browser` sample, still cycle 26. (4) task #122: the `0.21.34` prep, which carries the four prose copies of the publication samples.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 205 / a release record that names versions npm never had: the tag-time completeness gate, and four mutants that each died to the one test that names its leg

- **Milestone / version:** no release cut here; this lands as `0.21.34` material. Branch `feat/changelog-registry-completeness-gate`, rebased onto `main` at `3dbf52f` (PR #302), three commits — the gate, the step-prose update, and the far-side recount.
- **What the gate refuses.** `scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` now reads the packument's `time` map alongside the version/tag/CHANGELOG checks it already made, and fails the tag when the CHANGELOG names a release at or above `firstGatedRelease = 0.20.85` that the registry has never recorded. The release in flight is exempt by necessity (the step runs before the publish), duplicate sections report their hole once, and a failed registry read **warns and skips** rather than redding the release — the deliberate half of the design, because this repository has several gates that have already turned a good release red over their own plumbing.
- **Why a floor, from the measurement rather than from taste.** 40 of the CHANGELOG's 163 `## [x.y.z]` sections name versions with no registry `time` entry at all, and every one of them sits below `0.20.85`: `0.9.0`, each minor's first patch from `0.12.0` to `0.18.0`, **all ten** `0.19.x`, `0.20.0`–`0.20.5`, `0.20.54`, `0.20.55`, `0.20.69` and `0.20.72`–`0.20.84` — 1 + 7 + 10 + 6 + 2 + 1 + 13 = 40, with 27 of them carrying a git tag and 38 a roadmap delivered-scope block. The shorthand this bullet and the script header first carried (`0.12.0–0.20.5`) flattened 0.19's ten releases into a range that reads like two, and it was the arithmetic — not a re-read — that exposed it: a compressed enumeration has to sum to the count it is offered as the decomposition of. From `0.20.85` on the record is in lockstep (0.21.x measured 34 sections, 34 in the registry), so the gate can be strict about the era where strictness is the norm and cannot fire on the archaeology before it. Re-derive with `npm view cross-tab-worker-databus time --json`; the number that was current when this bullet was written is 46 gated releases, and the script prints its own count rather than letting a reader trust this one.
- **The kill table, with each mutant's own failing test named — the rule this repository wrote for itself.** Re-measured on the rebased tree, whole suite each time, literal line-targeted replacements, `applied=1` printed before each run, restore verified byte-identical with `git diff --quiet`: dropping the in-flight exemption fails exactly `exempts the release in flight, which cannot be published yet`; dropping the floor comparison fails exactly `leaves releases below the floor alone, because the hole predates the discipline`; dropping the duplicate-section dedupe fails exactly `reports a hole once even when its section is duplicated`; replacing the read-failure `return` with nothing (so the skip path falls through with `time` undefined) fails exactly `skips the completeness check rather than failing a release over a bad read`. One mutant, one test, every time — which is the point: the fourth is also the proof that the *skip* is a behavior and not an absence of one.
- **The rebase conflict was this repository's own, and resolving it was a measurement task.** `AGENTS.md` collided because #302 restructured the exact neighbourhood this branch had edited: main's side had removed a 1595-character paragraph that bullet 266 carried as a duplicate of bullet 267, and had re-attributed the Centrifuge no-op listener to `BaseSubscription`. Resolution took main's version (`git checkout --ours`) and re-applied this branch's single added sentence — the one about stating which side of a release a tally was taken on — then verified: 109 bullets, the duplicated paragraph's marker string present once, and `BaseSubscription` still there.
- **A new finding, recorded so it is not lost, and not yet fixed.** `rememberTopic()`'s eviction loop skips two candidates: `assignedTopics.has(candidate)` (documented, in three places) and `candidate === topicKey` — the key being remembered. The second term is undocumented anywhere in `src/` or `docs/`, and it is load-bearing because `Map.set` on an existing key keeps its **original** insertion position (verified: refreshing the front entry of `{a,b,c}` leaves `a` at the front), so re-remembering a topic that happens to be the oldest entry can otherwise evict the very mapping the caller is about to use — and `reconcileSubscriptions()` re-remembers every subscribed topic each cycle. Mutation probe on the committed tree: deleting the term leaves all 944 tests green, so it is **live and unpinned**, not dominated. The follow-up is a unit test that fills the reverse cache past `MAX_KNOWN_TOPICS` with unowned keys (inbound `CONTROL` frames are the natural source) and re-remembers the oldest. **Two halves of this bullet were wrong, and Phase 206 has the measurements: "undocumented anywhere in `docs/`" was false — `docs/architecture.md` and its zh mirror have carried a bullet naming the `topicKey` skip since the initial import (`8429d2f`), so the gap was in `src/` and in the tests only — and the follow-up as written cannot reach the term, because unowned keys are evicted before the scan ever gets to the fresh one, and because an inbound `CONTROL/SUBSCRIBE` produces *owned* entries rather than unowned ones.**
- **Verification:** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (37 files / **949** tests — 944 from main plus this branch's five gate cases), `pnpm lint` all green (`.gate-logs/gate-branch-final.log`). The gate itself was run against the live registry, not just the injected fixture: `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.33 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` prints the tag/version line and then `the 46 earlier CHANGELOG releases from 0.20.85 on are all in the registry's \`time\` map (0.21.33 is the release in flight and is exempt)`, exit 0. Mutation logs in `.gate-logs/mutant-gate/`.
- **Blockers:** none. **Risk / rollback:** the gate can only fail a tag when the CHANGELOG really does name an unpublished version, and it skips itself when the registry read fails, so its worst case is a warning. Reverting is a `git revert` of three commits; nothing published is touched.
- **Next:** (1) PR this branch, merge. (2) the `rememberTopic` eviction-guard test above, as its own change with its own Phase entry. (3) task #124 — raise the coordination sweep's `MAX_SEEDS` to 25,000 (measured: all 25,000 seeds green in ~47.5 s on an 8-core host at load 30, inside the 60 s sweep budget, so the cap rather than the clock is what limits a fast runner). (4) task #122 — `0.21.34` prep, now with both publication samples re-derived from the API (75.5 s gap, 304 s step) rather than transcribed.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 206 / the eviction skip that keeps the key being remembered, the doc rule that was already there, and the cap that does not bound an adoption flood

- **Milestone / version:** no release cut here; `0.21.34` material. Branch `test/known-topics-eviction-pin`, rebased onto `main` at `efdaf89` (PR #303, merged this cycle), one commit for the pin plus this entry.
- **What got pinned.** `WorkerClusterRuntime.rememberTopic()`'s eviction loop `continue`s past two candidates: `this.assignedTopics.has(candidate)` and `candidate === topicKey`. The second decided nothing any test could see — deleting it left all 944 tests green — so it was **live and unpinned**, not dominated. The reachable state is narrow and worth stating: a fresh `Map.set` goes to the **back**, so the front-scan only reaches the key it was called with once every older entry is owned, and there the mutant drops the very mapping the call exists to install. New case `keeps the topic it is remembering when the cache is full and every older entry is owned` builds exactly that: 500 peer `CONTROL/SUBSCRIBE` frames (adopted, therefore owned) fill the cache to the cap, then one `CONTROL/PUBLISH` (remembers without claiming) writes the 501st.
- **The kill table, one mutant per leg, both terms attributed.** `candidate === topicKey` → **one** failure, `keeps the topic it is remembering…`, at `AssertionError: expected [ 'owned.0', 'owned.1', …(498) ] to include 'evict.extra'` — the only test that names that term. `this.assignedTopics.has(candidate)` → **two**: the pre-existing `never evicts a topic the worker still owns from knownTopics` and the new one, which is the expected shape (the new setup owns everything, so it also observes the owned skip being lost). Logs in `.gate-logs/mutant-topickey-skip.log` and `.gate-logs/mutant-owned-skip.log`; each mutant printed `applied=1` before its run and `src/core/cluster.ts` was restored with `git checkout --` and re-grepped.
- **Two test designs that did not work, recorded because they are the reason the third one looks odd.** (1) Filling with 600 peer SUBSCRIBE frames produced no eviction at all: every adopted key is *owned*, so nothing is ever eligible and the cap just slips — the Phase 205 suggestion of filling "with unowned keys (inbound `CONTROL` frames are the natural source)" has this backwards, inbound SUBSCRIBE is the one frame type that cannot produce an unowned entry. (2) Re-remembering a key already in the cache cannot overflow anything, because `Map.set` on an existing key leaves `size` alone. The design that reaches the term is owned-prefix **plus** one new key.
- **The documentation half of the finding was wrong, and the correction is the more useful part.** Phase 205 recorded this term as "undocumented anywhere in `src/` or `docs/`". Only the `src/` half was true: `docs/architecture.md` has carried, since the initial import `8429d2f`, a bullet reading *"The entry being inserted is never evicted in the same step (`oldest !== topicKey` guard)"*, mirrored in zh. I was about to add a **third** statement of a rule the file already stated, in the one cell of the table that under-stated it. Two defects came out of actually reading the section: those bullets name a variable that does not exist (`oldest`; the code iterates `candidate` and `continue`s on **equality**, not inequality), which is the fake-identifier cousin of the decayed line number, and `docs/architecture.md:230`'s cap sentence was a security absolute the code does not provide.
- **The absolute, measured.** It claimed the cap "prevents a misbehaving or malicious peer from exhausting memory by referencing arbitrary topics in control messages". A same-origin script posting `CONTROL/SUBSCRIBE` for arbitrary topics is not stopped by it, because each frame is *adopted* and adoption makes the key unevictable: 1,200 frames grew `knownTopics` to 1,200 entries along with `assignedTopics` (marks at 500 / 600 / 800 / 1,200 each read `known == n`), and one `runIntervals()` took both to `0`. So the bound on that flood is the reconcile sweep — which is the durability property the `handleControlMessage` comment already argues for — while `MAX_KNOWN_TOPICS` bounds entries this worker does not own. Both languages now say which structure bounds which, and `src/core/cluster.ts`'s constant comment points at the loop instead of restating the leak claim. `DedupManager`'s "cannot exhaust memory" was checked against the same question and **holds**: its eviction loop has no skip term, so the FIFO there is unconditional.
- **Verification:** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (37 files / **945** tests — 944 from `main` plus this branch's one case), `pnpm lint` all green on the pre-rebase tree at `3dbf52f` (`.gate-logs/eviction-pin.log`). On the rebased tree, with the doc corrections and #303's five gate cases included, the same four commands are green at **950** tests (`.gate-logs/eviction-pin-final.log`); the new case was also re-run alone there and passes with the tightened `toBe(ownedCount)` / `toBe(ownedCount + 1)` premises, which replaced the earlier `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual` form because a premise assertion that also passes when the eviction never ran asserts nothing.
- **Blockers:** none. **Risk / rollback:** one test, three comment/doc edits, no behavior change — `git revert` of the branch's commit removes all of it. The docs are the only place a reader learned the cap bounds a SUBSCRIBE flood, and that sentence was shipping in both languages.
- **Next:** (1) PR this branch, merge. (2) task #124 — raise the coordination sweep's `MAX_SEEDS` to 25,000. (3) task #122 — `0.21.34` prep with both publication samples re-derived from the API rather than transcribed.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 207 / a cap comment that named the wrong protection, two tests written and deleted because they duplicated coverage that already had names, and the sweep cap that stays at 5,000

- **Milestone / version:** no release cut here; `0.21.34` material. Branch `test/trace-pending-caps` from `main` at `553ab61` (PR #304, merged this cycle).
- **What was wrong.** `recordReceived()`'s comment said "Both caps prevent a single misbehaving topic from exhausting memory". Only one of them does. `MAX_PENDING_MESSAGES_PER_TOPIC` (256) is the per-topic depth bound; `MAX_PENDING_TOPICS` (1,000) is an **admission** gate for distinct topics, so its sentence described a protection the guard does not provide — a single quiet topic arriving after the window is full is the thing it refuses. Measured directly: 1,001 distinct topics leave 1,000 queues and the 1,001st is never created, while an already-admitted topic keeps appending to 256 regardless of how full the window is, and `topics` reaches 10,001 beside 1,000 queues. That last Set is capped by neither *on purpose* — it answers which topics were touched, which includes the ones admission refused — and what bounds it is the window flush, because both record paths increment a counted field before adding, so a window that grows it reaches `resetMetrics()`.
- **The two tests I wrote and then deleted, which is the part worth keeping.** The probe above looked like an unpinned leg, so I added `admits at most MAX_PENDING_TOPICS distinct topics per window…` and `queues at most MAX_PENDING_MESSAGES_PER_TOPIC timestamps for a single topic`. The mutation run answered: deleting the admission guard failed **two** tests — mine, and `caps the number of topics tracked for pending receives` at `expected 1001 to be 1000`. Both caps had been pinned all along (trace.test.ts lines 213 and 227), the existing cases with *more* inputs than mine (1,100 topics, and it asserts the touched/sampled pair my comment claimed was novel). So both new tests were deleted and the comment now names the two existing cases instead of asserting their absence. Same rule as a candidate harness's marginal kill rate, applied to a candidate test: the question is never "does this leg have a test" but "does any mutant die to *this* one alone".
- **Why my grep missed them, and the fix for the grep.** I searched `tests/trace.test.ts` for `MAX_PENDING|1_000\b` and got only unrelated `metricsIntervalMs: 1_000` hits, because the two tests are written with the *numeric literals in a comment* (`// MAX_PENDING_TOPICS = 1000`) and the loop bound `1_100`; neither name nor the constant appears in their code. Search for the number the leg produces (`dispatchSamples`) or for the test's own verb (`caps`), not for the constant it documents — a test can be named for a guard and still not mention its identifier.
- **The identifier table had the third copy of last cycle's eviction rule.** `docs/architecture.md`'s `knownTopics` row still read "FIFO-capped at 500; never evicts owned keys" (zh "FIFO 上限 500；永不淘汰拥有中的键") — written before the bounded-vs-slip correction merged in #304, and contradicting it. Both cells now state the scan, both skips, and the slipping cap. The `assignedTopics` row beside them listed only `CONTROL/UNSUBSCRIBE` and handoff as release paths, omitting `reconcileAssignedTopics` — which is precisely the leg that takes a 1,200-entry adoption flood back to `0`, so the row that should have been the reader's guide to the bound named the two paths that never fire in that scenario.
- **A process defect of my own, recorded because the rule already exists and I broke it anyway.** I edited the comment, *then* ran the mutation probe, and the probe's `git checkout -- src/core/trace.ts` restore reverted my uncommitted edit — the correction had to be re-typed. "Commit before mutating" is in `AGENTS.md` and in memory precisely because the restore is the last step of a probe and does not know what you meant to keep.
- **Decision on task #124 (raise the coordination sweep from 5,000 to 25,000 seeds): not taken, with the reason.** The 25,000-seed run is real (green in ~47.5 s) but it adds nothing to what the file already records — its own comment carries a 400,000-seed, 753.7 s sweep with no violation, so depth availability is not in question and the shipped cap is already documented as a CI-time compromise rather than a safety line. Raising it is a coupled change, not a constant: CI's coverage run clears 5,000 seeds in 27.6 s, so 25,000 needs the fuse above ~138 s and the `it()` ceiling above that (≈180 s), roughly doubling the `verify` job; keeping the 60 s fuse instead makes the truncation line print on *every* CI run, which destroys the one signal it was added to emit. The regression-detection argument also points the other way — the heaviest mutant this harness kills dies at seed 12. So: 5,000/60 s stay, and the deep sweep remains what you run on purpose, locally, by editing the three constants the comment names.
- **Verification:** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (37 files / **950** tests — unchanged, since this branch adds no test), `pnpm lint` all green (`.gate-logs/trace-caps-final.log`). The mutation log that produced the duplicate-test finding is kept at `.gate-logs/mutant-trace-admission.log`; `src/core/trace.ts` was restored and re-grepped (`MAX_PENDING_TOPICS) return` present once).
- **Blockers:** none. **Risk / rollback:** three comment/doc edits, no code behavior touched, no test added or removed on the final tree — `git revert` is the whole rollback.
- **Next:** (1) PR this branch, merge. (2) task #122 — `0.21.34` prep with both publication samples re-derived from the API rather than transcribed, now carrying #303's gate, #304's pin and this cycle's corrections.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 208 / 0.21.34 prepared: the completeness gate's first live run, and the count that changes on both sides of a tag

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.34` prepared, not yet tagged. Branch `chore/release-0.21.34`, four commits on `main` at `6ffbfdb` (PR #305) — the sample extension, the version/CHANGELOG/roadmap prep, this entry, and the `AGENTS.md` tally correction below — with `0.21.33` still the published latest (`time['0.21.33'] = 2026-09-25T00:32:35.519Z`).
- **The live-guidance copy of the duration tally was one release behind, and it is the bullet that warns about exactly that.** `AGENTS.md`'s publish-lag rule still read "seven green tag runs … 304–308 s (…then 308 s and 304 s under it)" while `0.21.33`'s 304 s made it eight. The sentence is the one that instructs the reader to write the *lookup* rather than the value, so the fix added the lookup in place ("take them from each run's `Verify published npm consumers` step rather than from this sentence, which is one release behind by construction") instead of only bumping the number.
- **What ships in it.** #303's release-record completeness gate (`scripts/verify-release-version.mjs`), #304's `rememberTopic` eviction-skip pin plus the bounded-vs-slip corrections to both architecture docs, and #305's trace cap-comment correction with its identifier-table fixes. Library code is untouched apart from comments; the suite moved 944 → 949 → 950 across those three.

Re-derived independently rather than read off the script: 164 `## [x.y.z]` sections in `CHANGELOG.md`, 47 of them at or above `0.20.85` and below the in-flight one, all present; 40 below the floor and absent from the registry, matching the enumeration the script header and this log both carry (1 + 7 + 10 + 6 + 2 + 1 + 13 = 40, `0.9.0` + seven minor-firsts + ten `0.19.x` + six `0.20.0`–`.5` + `0.20.54`/`0.20.55` + `0.20.69` + thirteen `0.20.72`–`.84`).

The missing-side count has the same hazard in the other direction: the file says 40 sections name unpublished versions, which is true *excluding* `0.21.34`, while including it the reading is 41 — and the exemption exists precisely because of that. Every copy of both figures in `CHANGELOG.md` and both roadmap languages now states the boundary ("41 counting the release in flight, which is why the gate exempts it") instead of leaving a reader to find which set was counted.

## Phase 210 / the case name that was really a fixture string: task #127 closed, and the citation class given a gate

- **Milestone / version:** no release cut here; this is `0.21.35` material (both corrected sentences sit in **shipped declarations**). Branch `docs/agents-cap-restatement` cut from `main` at `e98e6ed` (PR #307, the 0.21.34 record), rebased once and clean, four commits: the `AGENTS.md` cap restatement, the two citation fixes plus the gate, the scope widening, and the rule that came out of it.
- **Task #127, closed.** `AGENTS.md`'s opaque-key section — the copy that steers every future session — still said `knownTopics` is a "FIFO eviction, max 500 entries" cache that "never evicts a key the worker still owns", two releases after `src/` and both architecture languages were corrected. Both halves are now the measured statement: the 500 bound counts **entries this worker does not own**, the scan skips two candidates (the owned key, and the key being remembered, because a fresh `Map.set` lands at the back so the front-scan reaches it only in the all-owned state), and in that state the cap slips — 1,200 adopted peer `CONTROL/SUBSCRIBE` frames grew both maps to 1,200 and one reconcile tick returned them to 0. The sentence's own claim that "both are pinned by named cases" was checked rather than asserted: `'never evicts a topic the worker still owns from knownTopics'` and `'keeps the topic it is remembering when the cache is full and every older entry is owned'` are both present titles in `tests/cluster.test.ts`. Corpus after the edit: 353 lines / 110 top-level bullets (from 352 / 109), and the only test that references `AGENTS.md` is the new one, which reads it as text rather than counting it.
- **The finding the sweep turned up, and it is not the one it went looking for.** While re-deriving that section's citations, the question became the inverse of the drifted line number: a comment that cites a case *by name*, where the name is not a case name. `src/core/routing.ts` pointed at a case it named `sticky-existing-routes` and `src/core/trace.ts` at one it named `no-trace`. Neither is an `it()` title — each is a `clusterKey` literal written twice inside a test body (`grep -n "sticky-existing-routes" tests/cluster.test.ts`, `grep -n "no-trace" tests/data-bus.test.ts`; no line numbers here, because that is the class `AGENTS.md` already retires), so each pointer landed mid-body instead of at the assertion, and the first rename of either arbitrary fixture string would have landed nowhere. That is the same silent decay as `:79-82`, one level up, and with a worse failure mode: a stale line number still opens the right file, while a stale name reports "no matches" for a grep that looks authoritative. Both fixed to name the case (`'keeps existing topic owners and balances only newly introduced topics'`, `'keeps tracing disabled by default'`), and the claim that they *ship* was verified at the artifact rather than argued — after `pnpm build`, the new strings are in `dist/core/routing.d.ts` and `dist/core/trace.d.ts` and the old ones are not.
- **The class is gated now.** `tests/documentation.test.ts`'s "resolve to a case that exists in the file they name" scans every living prose surface — `src/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and the docs — and requires each `tests/…`'s 'name' citation to resolve to exactly **one** case in the file it names; a trailing ellipsis may prefix-match, but only against one. Scope was widened from `src`+`AGENTS.md` after measuring what the wider net costs rather than guessing: `docs/` carries 8 such citations and the only 4 in the tree that do not resolve are all in `docs/progress.md` (two are the fixture-token forms this change removes from `src/`, two quote a case by a truncated name with no ellipsis marking it as one), and `CHANGELOG.md`'s 3 are dated records — so `progress.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are exempt for the reason the shipped-docs guard already exempts `progress.md`, and the one `docs/` citation outside them (`architecture.md`) resolves. `README.md` carries zero citations today; it is in scope prospectively, and that is stated rather than implied by the file list.
- **Two controls, because both halves of a scan can go empty.** A title collector that matches nothing reports every citation dead; a citation pattern that matches nothing reports none — and an empty failure list reads as a clean bill either way. So the gate asserts it found the suite's titles (976 across 40 files at write time; the floor is 500, deliberately *not* the corpus size, because a floor at the current count reddens the moment a test file moves out of scope and teaches the next reader to lower it) and that it examined at least one citation (17 across 52 files, with the lookup printed at the site rather than the number trusted).
- **The kill table, each with its own failure named — the rule this repository wrote for itself.** Reverting the `routing.ts` citation to its fixture token: whole suite 37 files / 951 tests, exactly **1** failure, message `src/core/routing.ts cites tests/cluster.test.ts's "sticky-existing-routes" (0 matches)`. Replacing an `AGENTS.md` citation with a prefix that matches nine cases: `(9 matches)`, which is the ambiguity leg. Neutering the citation pattern → `the citation scan must examine at least one citation: expected 0 to be greater than 0`. Neutering the title collector → `the citation scan must find the suite case titles: expected 0 to be greater than 500`. Shortening the `docs/architecture.md` citation → 1 failure naming `docs/architecture.md`, which is the proof that the widened scope has teeth the `src`-only version did not. Logs: `.gate-logs/m1.log`, `m2.log`, `m2b.log`, `m3b.log`, `M4-ambiguous.log`, `m5.log`, and the discarded `m3.log` (the uncompiled mutant above). Two earlier legs in `M2-neuter-titles.log` / `M3-neuter-titles.log` never ran at all: the harness passed the replacement patterns through double quotes, so the shell ate the backslashes and the python `assert` for "did the edit land" fired before the suite did — the standing rule that an unapplied mutant reports as a green one, demonstrated by its own guard rather than by a reader who already knew it.
- **Three ways the instrument was wrong before it was right, and all three are the durable part.** The new gate's first run failed twelve legs on a tree that a standalone `node` script using the *identical* regex had just cleared — the destructure took capture group 2 (the quote character) instead of group 3 (the name), so every citation "resolved" to `'` or `"`. A gate you just wrote that contradicts a direct measurement is a broken instrument before it is a finding; the diff between the two runs is the whole diagnosis. Second: the first title-collector mutant replaced `\b(?:it|test)(?:\.\w+)*\(` with a version missing the backslash before `(`, so the file died at parse time — `Invalid regular expression … Unterminated group`, `Tests no tests` — which is the *uncompiled*-mutant class already recorded for `tsc` and the build, appearing one level down at the regex parser, and it reads as a kill in a summary line. Third, and the one that stung: after the gate was green and the rule written, the `AGENTS.md` bullet *describing the defect* named the two fixture tokens in citation form as examples, and `pnpm test` came back reporting exactly those two unresolved. An exemplum in citation form is indistinguishable from a live pointer — to the scanner and to the reader who greps it a year from now — so the rule now says to name the token bare when the sentence is about a defect rather than pointing at a case, and this entry writes both tokens bare for the same reason, even though `docs/progress.md` is the one file the scan is written to skip. All three are in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Scanner hygiene, since the first two drafts wasted more time than the finding took.** A loose "filename … quoted-string within 200 chars" window returned 41 "unmatched" citations, 40 of them parser artifacts (possessives, code snippets, prose); a stricter one returned 2 matches against 16 real citations. What made it usable was normalising the comment continuation (`\n` + `//` or `*`) into a space before comparing, and requiring the closer to be the *same* quote character. The scan that found this class was written to answer a different question — whether any citation pointed at a renamed test — and the answer was "no, but two pointed at things that were never names".
- **Changed files:** `AGENTS.md`, `src/core/routing.ts`, `src/core/trace.ts`, `tests/documentation.test.ts`, `docs/progress.md`.
- **Verification:** `pnpm lint` exit 0 and `pnpm check` exit 0 (typecheck, build, `pnpm test` at **37 files / 951 tests**, `pnpm test:perf` 5 passed) on the final tree, `.gate-logs/gate-citation-final.log`; `tests/documentation.test.ts` alone at 20 passed (was 19). `pnpm typecheck` caught one real defect during authoring — casting a `RegExpExecArray` to a 4-tuple is `TS2352` — which is the standing reminder that `vitest` transpiles `tests/**` with no type checking, so a broken test can be green locally and red in CI's `verify`.
- **Blockers:** none. **Risk / rollback:** the only new failure mode is the gate, which fires on a rename of a cited case or a move of a test file — the cheap fix is to update the citation, which is the point. `git revert` of the four commits restores the previous text; nothing published is touched by the revert itself, and the two corrected strings reappear in the next build's declarations if it is taken.
- **Next:** (1) PR this branch, merge. (2) `0.21.35` prep: extend both publication lists (nine ack→record gaps with `0.21.34`'s **75.8 s**, nine step durations with its **304 s**), expect the completeness gate to print **48**, and carry this phase's two declaration corrections plus the `AGENTS.md` restatement in the release note — `maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs` stays at 310 s because neither new sample beats it. (3) the standing `bench:browser` sample, still deferred against a loaded host. (4) the same citation question applied to *symbol* names in comments (`rememberTopic()`'s "three of six call sites" class), which the gate cannot see because a symbol may be inlined away.
- **Update date:** 2026-09-25


## Phase 211 / 0.21.35 prepared, and the release gate that called a published version unpublished from a read that succeeded

- **Milestone / version:** `0.21.35` **prepared**, not yet published. Branch `chore/release-0.21.35-prep` cut from `main` at `e98e6ed` (PR #307) and rebased onto `891fae8` (PR #308, task #127 plus the citation gate) before its own PR opened — the anchor rule is why it waited. Three commits: the publication samples, the registry fix, and the `AGENTS.md` rule that came out of it.
- **The defect, and it is the gate's *own* inference that broke.** `scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` refuses a tag when a CHANGELOG section names a version the registry never recorded, and its header justified the strictness with "`time[]` records never expire, so a version missing from a read that succeeded was never published". Run locally for this tag it exited 1 with `CHANGELOG names 1 release(s) the registry has never recorded: 0.21.34` — about a version npmjs had recorded at `02:47:50.782Z`, **3,207 s (53 min)** before the gate ran (`.gate-logs/release-35-gate.log` is stamped `03:41:18Z`). The host's `npm` is configured to `registry.npmmirror.com`; its packument still reported `modified: 2026-09-25T00:32:51.767Z`, the `0.21.33` publish — and re-reading the mirror 13 minutes later showed `modified` had moved to `03:44:48.778Z`, i.e. **3,418 s** after the record, with the failing gate sitting **210 s** before that sync. **The first draft of that whole passage said `75 minutes`, and no pair of these stamps produces it:** the two previous-release stamps are 8,099 s (135 min) apart, and the real staleness window was 3,418 s. So the honest statement is that the figure's origin is unrecoverable — it reads as arithmetic on whatever numbers were on screen, which is exactly the failure the 'name the series attached to the number' rule exists to stop, reached here by writing the sentence from memory of the timestamps instead of from them. Fixed in seven copies by grepping the phrase, each with the subtraction that produces the number written beside it; the `CHANGELOG.md` sentence that also says `seventh` is about `0.21.33`, where it is correct, so it stands. So the sentence was true in both of its stated halves and false in an unstated one: the read succeeded, and `time[]` entries do not expire, but *a document that has not learned of a version is not a record of its absence*. Confirmed by reading both sources with `cache-control: no-cache`: npmjs answers `0.21.34 → 02:47:50.782Z`, `latest = 0.21.34`, 124 time keys; the mirror answers `0.21.34 → None`, `latest = 0.21.33`, 123. **A mirror's sync lag is not HTTP caching, so no cache-busting header rescues it** — only naming the registry does. The read now passes `--registry https://registry.npmjs.org`, and the documented re-derive command in both checklist languages carried the unpinned form, which is how the wrong instruction had already propagated into prose.
- **Why no test saw it, which is the more transferable half.** Every case in `tests/release-version.test.ts` injects `RELEASE_REGISTRY_TIME`; the stub short-circuits `readRegistryTime` before it can choose a registry, so *the decision under test was never executed by any test*. A gate whose whole suite stubs the value it audits is silent about how the real one is obtained. The new case runs the un-injected path: a stub `npm` on `PATH` records its own argv, the script is spawned with `RELEASE_REGISTRY_TIME` deleted, and the assertions check that `--registry` and the URL arrive **as a pair** rather than checking the URL appears somewhere. Three mutants, three different assertions: dropping both args dies at `the gate called npm without naming a registry: view cross-tab-worker-databus time --json`, pointing it at the mirror dies at `expected 'https://registry.npmmirror.com' to be 'https://registry.npmjs.org'`, and passing the URL without the flag dies at the *first* message — which is what says the pair check is a behavior and not a substring match. `verify-published-consumer.mjs` had pinned `--registry` on both of its reads for this same reason; this was the last npm-based registry read in the repository that did not, and the sibling's comment already said "Naming `--registry` explicitly does not defeat the local cache".
- **The gate re-run live, after the fix.** `RELEASE_TAG=v0.21.35 node scripts/verify-release-version.mjs` exits 0 and prints `the 48 earlier CHANGELOG releases from 0.20.85 on are all in the registry's time map (0.21.35 is the release in flight and is exempt)` — 48 where `0.21.34`'s tag printed 47, exactly the rise Phase 209 predicted, and the reason the count is quoted from the script's own line rather than from prose.
- **The publication samples, extended in all four copies.** `0.21.34`'s tag run: `Publish to npm` completed `02:46:35Z`, registry record `02:47:50.782Z` (**75.8 s**), `Verify published npm consumers` **304 s** — the eighth ack→record reading and the ninth green step duration. Neither beats the derivation: 75.8 s < 310 s, so `maxMeasuredAckToRecordMs` and `PUBLISHED_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS=96` stay, and the floor test passes unmodified. What the widened set *did* produce is a separation the earlier samples could not make: the three newest records — 76.1, 75.5, 75.8 s across three consecutive releases — span **0.6 s**, while the step consumed 304 s each time. That puts the variance in the reader and not in the write, and it is now stated in both checklist languages, the workflow comment and `tests/workflows.test.ts` beside the `gh api` lookup that re-derives it. Both enumerations were re-counted from the sentences themselves (8 gaps, and 5 + 1 + 3 durations under the "each" form) rather than trusted to the adjective.
- **An ordinal in this file's own record, corrected where it stands.** Phase 209 wrote that `0.21.34`'s 75.8 s was "the seventh value in that list"; the list already carried seven (through `0.21.33`), so it is the eighth. Its sibling claim — "the ninth green sample in the 304–308 s band" — was right, which is the argument for re-deriving each half of a pair separately. The published `CHANGELOG.md` sentence that reads "seventh ack→`time[<version>]` reading" is about `0.21.33` and is correct, so it stands untouched; the correction went into Phase 209 in place, naming this phase as its source, because a dated record may keep its date but not a wrong count that a later entry will copy forward.
- **A suite count that moved twice inside one cycle, and was corrected by re-running rather than by adding.** `AGENTS.md`'s release-budget bullet said "eight green tag runs … 308 s, 304 s and 304 s"; it now says nine and carries the fourth `304 s`, with the same "one release behind by construction" caveat that made the staleness visible rather than concealed. The prep commit first wrote "37 files / 951 tests", which was true of the tree before the registry case existed and false after it and after the rebase onto #308; the shipped text says **952**, taken from `pnpm test` on the rebased tree. `AGENTS.md` is now 355 lines / 111 bullets, and #308's citation gate passes on the prose this phase added — the new bullets mention `tests/release-version.test.ts` non-possessively, which is exactly the form the scan is written to ignore.
- **Verification:** `pnpm lint` exit 0 and `pnpm check` exit 0 (37 files / 951 tests at that point, perf green) on the pre-rebase tree, `.gate-logs/gate-prep-35.log`; `pnpm test` on the rebased tree at **37 files / 952 tests**, `.gate-logs/` as noted; `pnpm typecheck` clean. One real defect caught by the compiler and not by the suite, as usual: the stub's `env` object literal collapsed its index signature, so `delete env.RELEASE_REGISTRY_TIME` was `TS2339` while `vitest run` passed it happily — the same asymmetry this file has recorded before. Mutation logs: `.gate-logs/R1-drop-pair.log`, `R2-wrong-registry.log`, `R3-url-only.log`; two earlier legs reported `MUTANT NOT APPLIED` from a shell-quoting mistake in the harness before the third form was fixed, and neither was counted as a result.
- **Blockers:** none. **Risk / rollback:** the registry pin can only *reduce* false refusals — a read that fails still skips, so a machine that cannot reach npmjs behaves exactly as before. The release itself is not published, so rollback of this branch is an ordinary revert; if it merges and the tag is cut, `0.21.36` supersedes forward.
